 14876	## BLOCKER
 14877	
 14878	**`FieldView.deck` is a good projection, but it cannot be the knowledge model or its source of truth.**
 14879	
 14880	`PlayerView` is rebuilt from `GameState`, yet `PlayerState` stores only zone contents and has no knowledge state (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:16`). `viewFor` can currently derive only the viewer’s hand and public zones (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:17`, `packages/engine/src/view.ts:21`). After Reeve bottoms two known cards, a later `viewFor` has no record that its controller still knows those bottom positions. Worse, a root view must preserve that the opponent knows those sampled positions without revealing their identities to root; `(CardId | null)[]` cannot express “unknown to me, known to them.” The fixed-order mulligan already creates private known bottom cards (`packages/engine/src/setup.ts:70`).
 14881	
 14882	Miner also proves knowledge is not deck-only: its publicly revealed chosen Backup enters a hidden hand (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:151`), but the opponent retains its identity; `FieldView` records only `handCount`, and `PlayerView.hand` represents only `me` (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:5`, `packages/engine/src/view.ts:8`).
 14883	
 14884	**Fix:** Store knowledge durably in `GameState`, preferably as a compact per-card `knownBy` bitmask separate from `CardInstance`. Project deck slots as `{ card: CardId | null, knownBy: mask }`, or parallel `deck` and `deckKnownBy` arrays. Add a known-opponent-hand multiset and record which of the viewer’s hand cards the opponent knows. Public deck lists eliminate uncertainty about the declared multiset, not about positions or the hand/deck partition.
 14885	
 14886	---
 14887	
 14888	**C3-2 does not perform the candidate rebinding required by the D2 review.**
 14889	
 14890	Today determinisation gathers public zones plus the root hand (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:37`), removes those codes (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:39`), shuffles everything remaining (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:40`), mints both decks anew (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:41`, `packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:44`), then blindly copies `pending` and `resolution` (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:49`). Redacting an opponent’s Reeve candidates therefore leaves no executable candidates; copying an authorized pending works only because pinned IDs happen to survive.
 14891	
 14892	This is exactly the unresolved requirement named by C2 and the D2 review (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c2-observer-triggers.md:107`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-code-review.md:7203`). A redacted `Pending` also cannot serve as live state: engine invariants require `max <= candidates.length` and every candidate to exist (`packages/engine/src/invariants.ts:62`).
 14893	
 14894	**Fix:** Split `PendingState` from `PendingView`. In `determinise`:
 14895	
 14896	1. Include public IDs, root hand, known opponent-hand IDs, and non-null deck slots in the fixed set.
 14897	2. Remove each fixed code once from the declared multiset.
 14898	3. Sample the unknown opponent-hand count.
 14899	4. Fill only null deck indices, leaving pinned indices untouched.
 14900	5. Reconstruct the internal deck-choice pending from the active AST and the sampled deck—never copy redacted candidates.
 14901	6. Recreate the knowledge masks, including opponent-known/root-unknown sampled positions.
 14902	
 14903	Pins then come exclusively from the view. That creates no extra AI information; consulting the live deck or raw ground-truth pending during projection would.
 14904	
 14905	---
 14906	
 14907	**C3-4 fixes the root-history leak by replacing the opponent’s choice with a random policy.**
 14908	
 14909	The collapse does not merge different root information sets—the root genuinely cannot distinguish the private choices. It does merge different actions available to the informed opponent. Search groups commands sharing a key and randomly chooses one from the group (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:386`, `packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:398`). Collapsing all Reeve selections therefore makes the opponent pick uniformly, repeating the defect the existing actor-view keying explicitly avoids (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:372`).
 14910	
 14911	One key also cannot serve both roles. Root’s own Reeve alternatives must remain distinguishable, but deck IDs currently have no canonical references (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:147`), so every root deck target becomes `?` at `chooseTargets` (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:227`) and the final search rejects the opaque key (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:438`). Known deck contents are also absent from `ObservationKey`, which hashes only deck count (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:395`).
 14912	
 14913	**Fix:** Separate:
 14914	
 14915	- an actor/policy key, naming a known deck choice by semantic code and merging interchangeable copies; and
 14916	- an observer transition key, collapsed only when `actor !== root` and the action is private.
 14917	
 14918	For SO-ISMCTS, resolve the concrete command under that collapsed edge with a deterministic actor policy, not random grouping. If private opponent choices must themselves be searched with UCT, that requires multi-observer/player information-set nodes, not a special `ActionKey`.
 14919	
 14920	Implement the distinction around `buildIndex` (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:147`), the `chooseTargets` case (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:227`), and the deck/pending observation digests (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:395`, `packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:437`). C3-A4 is insufficient; also assert root-known deck changes split observations, opponent-private identities do not, and collapsed commands are not chosen randomly.
 14921	
 14922	---
 14923	
 14924	**Redacting `pending.candidates` alone still leaks Reeve through the browser log and leaves the agenda as an unchecked raw-ID channel.**
 14925	
 14926	`PlayerView` carries `resolution` wholesale under the now-invalid assertion that every ID in it is public (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:9`). `Frame.chosen` is an unrestricted `CardId[]` (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:143`). The proposed cards can avoid an agenda leak only if looked-at IDs live solely in `PendingState` while suspended and the private choice settles atomically before another prompt; the spec never establishes that invariant.
 14927	
 14928	The definite leak is the log: AI commands are deliberately described using the AI’s own view (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:222`, `apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:228`). `describeChoice` names every chosen target (`apps/web/src/game/commands.ts:241`). An AI Reeve choice would therefore tell the human exactly which card it took.
 14929	
 14930	`attack` is safe: its IDs name public field cards (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:26`, `packages/engine/src/view.ts:24`). Events are not in `PlayerView`, but any new reveal/move event containing private IDs would create another audience-blind channel.
 14931	
 14932	**Fix:** Define observer-safe `PendingView` and `ResolutionView`, or enforce and test that no private deck ID can survive in a visible `Frame`. Narrate AI choices from the human/observer view: private Reeve becomes “adds a card to hand,” while public Miner may name the selection. Emit identity-bearing reveal events only for public reveals.
 14933	
 14934	## MAJOR
 14935	
 14936	**The model must preserve what the other player knows, not merely what the current viewer knows.**
 14937	
 14938	After an opponent resolves Reeve, root does not know the bottom cards, but does know that the opponent knows them. A root determinisation must sample those identities and mark them visible in later `searchView(state, opponent)` calls. Otherwise the simulated opponent forgets information the real opponent retained. The current search explicitly builds actor views for opponent decisions (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:385`).
 14939	
 14940	**Fix:** Carry viewer-safe knowledge ownership metadata through `PlayerView`: identities only where visible to `me`, but positional `knownBy` masks even where the identity is null. Add an acceptance test that different determinizations sample different opponent-known bottom cards while the simulated opponent sees its sampled cards and root does not.
 14941	
 14942	---
 14943	
 14944	**Deck knowledge updates need centralized zone operations before Hugh Yurg or EX Burst.**
 14945	
 14946	Top removal is duplicated across setup deals (`packages/engine/src/setup.ts:56`), normal draws (`packages/engine/src/phases.ts:10`), and damage (`packages/engine/src/rules.ts:16`). Each must shift positional knowledge and carry known identity into the destination. A future search shuffle must clear positional pins. EX Burst already moves the top card into a public zone before its skipped effect (`packages/engine/src/rules.ts:22`), so its information rule is simple if those operations are centralized.
 14947	
 14948	**Fix:** Add deck primitives for `takeTop`, `moveToBottom`, and `shuffleDeck`. Move knowledge with cards; mark public reveals known to both; clear all deck-position knowledge on shuffle. Keep Hugh’s whole-deck search as a separate effect because its optional search, shuffle, put-onto-field destination, and resulting ETB triggers are not `lookAt(top N)`.
 14949	
 14950	---
 14951	
 14952	**A public Miner reveal is not currently visible in the browser while the AI chooses.**
 14953	
 14954	The board renders only deck count (`apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:57`) and displays off-board cards only when they are targets in the human’s own choice set (`apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:89`, `apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:141`). While AI Miner is choosing, the human has no such target choices, so the five publicly revealed cards will not appear.
 14955	
 14956	**Fix:** Render currently known/revealed deck slots independently of `choices.byCard`, or add a public reveal log/event listing all five. Add a browser test for AI Miner, not only human Miner/Reeve reachability.
 14957	
 14958	## MINOR
 14959	
 14960	**The fixed bottoming order is defensible, but it is strategically meaningful rather than cosmetic.**
 14961	
 14962	It does not change deck size, and deck-out is checked only when drawing or taking damage (`packages/engine/src/phases.ts:12`, `packages/engine/src/rules.ts:18`). It can still change later draws, damage cards, and future EX Bursts. The engine already makes the analogous fixed-order mulligan deviation (`packages/engine/src/setup.ts:74`). Current invariants check placement and uniqueness, not ordering (`packages/engine/src/invariants.ts:24`).
 14963	
 14964	**Fix:** Keep C3-6, describe it as a gameplay deviation, and test exact near-empty deck order plus aligned knowledge masks. A future shuffle must erase those pins.
 14965	
 14966	---
 14967	
 14968	**Miner plus Reeve is the right pair; Reeve alone is the cheapest card that forces the D2 information problem.**
 14969	
 14970	Reeve forces private positions and a private opponent action (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:181`). Miner adds the necessary public contrast and, importantly, the known-opponent-hand case (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:151`). Hugh Yurg additionally needs optional whole-deck search, shuffle, free field entry, and observer ETB dispatch (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:211`); current field-entry dispatch only finds abilities on the entering card itself (`packages/engine/src/cast.ts:54`). Cloud still needs phase-entry splitting and source-aware return protection (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:227`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c2-observer-triggers.md:100`).
 14971	
 14972	**Fix:** Keep Miner and Reeve; do not pull Hugh Yurg or Cloud into C3.
 14973	
 14974	---
 14975	
 14976	**One top-deck inspection primitive with an audience flag is sound for these two cards.**
 14977	
 14978	Both cards share inspect, choose, move one to hand, and bottom the rest (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-deck-knowledge.md:23`). The difference really is audience, count, and filter.
 14979	
 14980	**Fix:** Make the AST explicit about `audience`, destination, and remainder policy; do not generalize it into Hugh Yurg’s whole-deck search.

 15047	`PlayerView` carries `resolution` wholesale under the now-invalid assertion that every ID in it is public (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:9`). `Frame.chosen` is an unrestricted `CardId[]` (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:143`). The proposed cards can avoid an agenda leak only if looked-at IDs live solely in `PendingState` while suspended and the private choice settles atomically before another prompt; the spec never establishes that invariant.
 15048	
 15049	The definite leak is the log: AI commands are deliberately described using the AI’s own view (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:222`, `apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:228`). `describeChoice` names every chosen target (`apps/web/src/game/commands.ts:241`). An AI Reeve choice would therefore tell the human exactly which card it took.
 15050	
 15051	`attack` is safe: its IDs name public field cards (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:26`, `packages/engine/src/view.ts:24`). Events are not in `PlayerView`, but any new reveal/move event containing private IDs would create another audience-blind channel.
 15052	
 15053	**Fix:** Define observer-safe `PendingView` and `ResolutionView`, or enforce and test that no private deck ID can survive in a visible `Frame`. Narrate AI choices from the human/observer view: private Reeve becomes “adds a card to hand,” while public Miner may name the selection. Emit identity-bearing reveal events only for public reveals.
 15054	
 15055	## MAJOR
 15056	
 15057	**The model must preserve what the other player knows, not merely what the current viewer knows.**
 15058	
 15059	After an opponent resolves Reeve, root does not know the bottom cards, but does know that the opponent knows them. A root determinisation must sample those identities and mark them visible in later `searchView(state, opponent)` calls. Otherwise the simulated opponent forgets information the real opponent retained. The current search explicitly builds actor views for opponent decisions (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:385`).
 15060	
 15061	**Fix:** Carry viewer-safe knowledge ownership metadata through `PlayerView`: identities only where visible to `me`, but positional `knownBy` masks even where the identity is null. Add an acceptance test that different determinizations sample different opponent-known bottom cards while the simulated opponent sees its sampled cards and root does not.
 15062	
 15063	---
 15064	
 15065	**Deck knowledge updates need centralized zone operations before Hugh Yurg or EX Burst.**
 15066	
 15067	Top removal is duplicated across setup deals (`packages/engine/src/setup.ts:56`), normal draws (`packages/engine/src/phases.ts:10`), and damage (`packages/engine/src/rules.ts:16`). Each must shift positional knowledge and carry known identity into the destination. A future search shuffle must clear positional pins. EX Burst already moves the top card into a public zone before its skipped effect (`packages/engine/src/rules.ts:22`), so its information rule is simple if those operations are centralized.

Keep Hugh’s whole-deck search as a separate effect because its optional search, shuffle, put-onto-field destination, and resulting ETB triggers are not `lookAt(top N)`.
 15070	
 15071	---
 15072	
 15073	**A public Miner reveal is not currently visible in the browser while the AI chooses.**
 15074	
 15075	The board renders only deck count (`apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:57`) and displays off-board cards only when they are targets in the human’s own choice set (`apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:89`, `apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:141`). While AI Miner is choosing, the human has no such target choices, so the five publicly revealed cards will not appear.

 15078

 15080	
 15081	**The fixed bottoming order is defensible, but it is strategically meaningful rather than cosmetic.**

 15083	It does not change deck size, and deck-out is checked only when drawing or taking damage (`packages/engine/src/phases.ts:12`, `packages/engine/src/rules.ts:18`).  15088

 15090	
 15091	Reeve forces private positions and a private opponent action (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:181`).  15093	**Fix:** Keep Miner and Reeve; do not pull Hugh Yurg or Cloud into C3.

 15100	
 15101	**Fix:** Make the AST explicit about `audience`, destination, and remainder policy; do not generalize it into Hugh Yurg’s whole-deck search.

     8	/** §11.2.1.1/§11.2.2: a pure Light or pure Dark card needs no CP of its own element — its cost may be paid entirely
     9	 *  with off-element CP. Every other card (including a Light/Dark card combined with another element, none in the
    10	 *  MVP0 pool) still requires ≥1 CP of each of its listed elements. Callers pass this — not `def.elements` directly
    11	 *  — to `canPay` and to `preferredPayment`'s required-element phase. */
    12	export function requiredElements(def: CardDef): Element[] {
    13	  if (def.elements.length === 1 && (def.elements[0] === 'light' || def.elements[0] === 'dark')) return []
    14	  return def.elements
    15	}

    17	export interface GeneratedCp { element: Element; source: CardId }

    19	/** Validate the sources and compute the CP they generate. Throws IllegalCommandError on a bad source. */
    20	export function generateCp(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, payment: Payment, casting: CardId): GeneratedCp[] {
    21	  const ps = state.players[player]
    22	  const cp: GeneratedCp[] = []
    23	  const seen = new Set<CardId>()
    24	  for (const id of payment.dullBackups) {
    25	    const b = ps.backups.find((c) => c.id === id)
    26	    if (!b) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${id} is not a backup you control`)
    27	    if (b.status !== 'active') throw new IllegalCommandError(`backup ${id} is already dull`)
    28	    if (seen.has(id)) throw new IllegalCommandError(`backup ${id} used twice`)
    29	    seen.add(id)
    30	    const def = defOf(state, id)
    31	    cp.push({ element: def.elements[0] as Element, source: id })   // MVP0-SIMPLIFICATION: multi-element backups produce their first element; none in pool
    32	  }
    33	  for (const { card, element } of payment.discards) {
    34	    if (card === casting) throw new IllegalCommandError('cannot discard the card being cast')
    35	    if (!ps.hand.includes(card)) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${card} is not in your hand`)
    36	    if (seen.has(card)) throw new IllegalCommandError(`card ${card} discarded twice`)
    37	    seen.add(card)
    38	    const def = defOf(state, card)
    39	    if (def.elements.includes('light') || def.elements.includes('dark')) throw new IllegalCommandError('Light/Dark cards cannot be discarded for CP (§11.2.1.1)')
    40	    if (!def.elements.includes(element)) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${card} cannot produce ${element} CP`)
    41	    cp.push({ element, source: card }, { element, source: card })
    42	  }
    43	  return cp
    44	}
    45	
    46	/** §11.2.2.2–3: total ≥ cost, ≥1 CP of each of the card's elements; cost 0 → no CP may be generated (§11.2.2.4). */
    47	export function canPay(cost: number, elements: Element[], cp: GeneratedCp[]): boolean {
    48	  if (cost === 0) return cp.length === 0   // §11.2.2.4 / §11.2.2.1 last sentence
    49	  if (cp.length < cost) return false
    50	  // `elements` is expected to already be `requiredElements(def)` (Light/Dark exemption applied by the caller).
    51	  return elements.every((e) => cp.some((c) => c.element === e))   // §11.2.2.1–2
    52	}
    53	
    54	/** Every *minimal* legal payment for `card` (no source can be removed and still pay). Used by legalCommands as the canonical choice list; `apply` accepts any payment that `canPay` — overpaying is legal (§11.2.2.3). */
    55	export function enumeratePayments(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, card: CardId): Payment[] {
    56	  const def = defOf(state, card)
    57	  if (def.cost === 0) return [{ dullBackups: [], discards: [] }]
    58	  const elements = requiredElements(def)
    59	  const ps = state.players[player]
    60	  const backups = ps.backups.filter((b) => b.status === 'active').map((b) => b.id)
    61	  const discardOptions = ps.hand
    62	    .filter((id) => id !== card)
    63	    .flatMap((id) => defOf(state, id).elements.filter((e) => e !== 'light' && e !== 'dark').map((element) => ({ card: id, element })))
    64	  // Each hand card may be discarded at most once, so choose ≤1 element option per card.
    65	  const byCard = new Map<CardId, Element[]>()
    66	  for (const o of discardOptions) byCard.set(o.card, [...(byCard.get(o.card) ?? []), o.element])
    67	  const handCards = [...byCard.keys()]
    68	
    69	  const results: Payment[] = []
    70	  const nBackupSubsets = 1 << backups.length
    71	  const choices = handCards.map((c) => byCard.get(c) as Element[])
    72	  // iterate over backup subsets × per-card choice (none | element_i)
    73	  const walk = (i: number, discards: Payment['discards'], backupMask: number) => {
    74	    if (i === handCards.length) {
    75	      const dullBackups = backups.filter((_, k) => backupMask & (1 << k))
    76	      const payment = { dullBackups, discards }
    77	      const cp = generateCp(state, player, payment, card)
    78	      if (!canPay(def.cost, elements, cp)) return
    79	      // minimality: removing any single source must break payment
    80	      for (let k = 0; k < dullBackups.length; k++) {
    81	        const less = { ...payment, dullBackups: dullBackups.filter((_, j) => j !== k) }
    82	        if (canPay(def.cost, elements, generateCp(state, player, less, card))) return
    83	      }
    84	      for (let k = 0; k < discards.length; k++) {
    85	        const less = { ...payment, discards: discards.filter((_, j) => j !== k) }
    86	        if (canPay(def.cost, elements, generateCp(state, player, less, card))) return
    87	      }
    88	      results.push(payment)
    89	      return
    90	    }
    91	    walk(i + 1, discards, backupMask)
    92	    for (const element of choices[i] as Element[]) walk(i + 1, [...discards, { card: handCards[i] as CardId, element }], backupMask)
    93	  }
    94	  for (let mask = 0; mask < nBackupSubsets; mask++) walk(0, [], mask)
    95	  return results
    96	}

    98	/** Execute a payment. INTERNAL — callers must have run generateCp + canPay first (cast.ts does). */
    99	export function pay(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, payment: Payment): [GameState, Event[]] {
   100	  const events: Event[] = []
   101	  const s = updatePlayer(state, player, (ps) => ({
   102	    ...ps,
   103	    backups: ps.backups.map((b) => (payment.dullBackups.includes(b.id) ? { ...b, status: 'dull' } : b)),
   104	    hand: ps.hand.filter((id) => !payment.discards.some((d) => d.card === id)),
   105	    breakZone: [...ps.breakZone, ...payment.discards.map((d) => d.card)],
   106	  }))
   107	  for (const d of payment.discards) events.push({ type: 'discarded', player, card: d.card, reason: 'cp' })
   108	  const cp = [...payment.dullBackups.map((id) => defOf(state, id).elements[0] as Element), ...payment.discards.flatMap((d) => [d.element, d.element])]
   109	  events.unshift({ type: 'cpGenerated', player, cp })
   110	  return [s, events]
   111	}

    89	  const damaged = h.victim !== null ? h.victim : h.target === null ? null : findFieldCard(state, h.target)?.owner ?? null
    90	  if (damaged === null) return true   // nothing attributable to compare against
    91	  return whose === 'self' ? damaged === h.sourceController : damaged === opponentOf(h.sourceController)
    92	}
    93	
    94	/** The clause a frame is executing, or null if the def no longer declares it (a hot-swapped card pool). */
    95	export function abilityOf(state: GameState, frame: Frame): Ability | null {
    96	  const code = state.cards[frame.source]?.code
    97	  const def = code === undefined ? undefined : state.defs[code]
    98	  return def?.abilities?.find((a) => a.id === frame.abilityId) ?? null
    99	}
   100	
   101	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   102	// Targeting
   103	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   104	
   105	function defFor(state: GameState, id: CardId) {
   106	  const code = state.cards[id]?.code
   107	  return code === undefined ? undefined : state.defs[code]
   108	}
   109	
   110	function matchesFilter(state: GameState, source: CardId, id: CardId, filter: TargetFilter | undefined): boolean {
   111	  if (!filter) return true
   112	  const def = defFor(state, id)
   113	  if (!def) return false
   114	  if (filter.type !== undefined && def.type !== filter.type) return false
   115	  // "Character" is Forward, Backup OR Monster and never Summon (§7.2), which a single `type` cannot say — both
   116	  // Prishe's and Luso's Break-Zone retrievals need it (spec C2-9). `type` and `types` conjoin: a filter carrying
   117	  // both must satisfy both.
   118	  if (filter.types !== undefined && !filter.types.includes(def.type)) return false
   119	  if (filter.element !== undefined && !def.elements.includes(filter.element)) return false
   120	  if (filter.maxCost !== undefined && def.cost > filter.maxCost) return false
   121	  if (filter.excludeSource && id === source) return false
   122	  if (filter.excludeSourceName) {
   123	    const src = defFor(state, source)
   124	    if (src && src.name === def.name) return false
   125	  }
   126	  return true
   127	}
   128	
   129	/**
   130	 * The legal targets of one `TargetSpec`, in a fixed player-0-then-1 order so a live state and its
   131	 * determinisation enumerate the same candidates in the same order (spec C1-A6).
   132	 */
   133	export function targetCandidates(state: GameState, source: CardId, controller: PlayerId, spec: TargetSpec): CardId[] {
   134	  const owners: readonly PlayerId[] = spec.controller === 'any' ? [0, 1]
   135	    : spec.controller === 'self' ? [controller] : [opponentOf(controller)]
   136	  const out: CardId[] = []
   137	  for (const p of ([0, 1] as const).filter((q) => owners.includes(q))) {
   138	    const ps = state.players[p]
   139	    const ids = spec.zone === 'breakZone' ? ps.breakZone
   140	      : (spec.zone === 'forwards' ? ps.forwards : ps.backups).map((c) => c.id)
   141	    for (const id of ids) if (matchesFilter(state, source, id, spec.filter)) out.push(id)
   142	  }
   143	  return out
   144	}
   145	
   146	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147	// Zone plumbing
   148	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   149	
   150	function setFieldCard(state: GameState, id: CardId, f: (c: FieldCard) => FieldCard): GameState {
   151	  const loc = findFieldCard(state, id)
   152	  if (!loc) return state
   153	  return updatePlayer(state, loc.owner, (ps) => (loc.zone === 'forwards'
   154	    ? { ...ps, forwards: ps.forwards.map((c) => (c.id === id ? f(c) : c)) }
   155	    : { ...ps, backups: ps.backups.map((c) => (c.id === id ? f(c) : c))}))
   156	}
   157	
   158	function removeFromField(state: GameState, id: CardId): GameState {
   159	  const loc = findFieldCard(state, id)
   160	  if (!loc) return state
   161	  return updatePlayer(state, loc.owner, (ps) => (loc.zone === 'forwards'
   162	    ? { ...ps, forwards: ps.forwards.filter((c) => c.id !== id) }
   163	    : { ...ps, backups: ps.backups.filter((c) => c.id !== id) }))
   164	}
   165	
   166	/** §7.10: a card always goes to its OWNER's zone, not its controller's. Returns null if the card is nowhere movable. */
   167	function toHand(state: GameState, id: CardId): GameState | null {
   168	  const owner = state.cards[id]?.owner
   169	  if (owner === undefined) return null
   170	  let s = state
   171	  if (findFieldCard(state, id)) s = removeFromField(s, id)
   172	  else {
   173	    const holder = ([0, 1] as const).find((p) => state.players[p].breakZone.includes(id))
   174	    if (holder === undefined) return null
   175	    s = updatePlayer(s, holder, (ps) => ({ ...ps, breakZone: ps.breakZone.filter((x) => x !== id) }))
   176	  }
   177	  return updatePlayer(s, owner, (ps) => ({ ...ps, hand: [...ps.hand, id] }))
   178	}
   179	
   180	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181	// The walker
   182	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   183	
   184	interface Ctx {
   185	  state: GameState
   186	  events: Event[]
   187	  source: CardId
   188	  controller: PlayerId
   189	  abilityId: string
   190	  /** Program counter, one index per nesting level. `chooseModes` owns TWO levels: mode ordinal, then effect index. */
   191	  path: number[]
   192	  chosen: CardId[]
   193	  modes: number[]
   194	  /** What fired this clause, for `onSubject` and narration; null for self-triggers (spec C2-5). */
   195	  triggerEvent: TriggerEvent | null
   196	  /** The path the frame was suspended at; execution rejoins it instead of replaying the effects already run. */
   197	  resume: readonly number[]
   198	  suspend: Pending | null
   199	  steps: number
   200	}
   201	
   202	/**
   203	 * Spec C1-5: every effect step is counted, the count lives on `GameState` and therefore PERSISTS across player
   204	 * choices. A call-depth cap would not see a trigger cycle that launders itself through a `chooseTargets` prompt.
   205	 */
   206	function step(ctx: Ctx): void {
   207	  ctx.steps++
   208	  if (ctx.steps > MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS) {
   209	    throw new Error(`ability ${ctx.abilityId} on card ${ctx.source} exceeded ${MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS} resolution steps (spec C1-5) — trigger cycle?`)
   210	  }
   211	}
   212	
   213	function noLegalTarget(ctx: Ctx): void {
   214	  // Spec C1-7: an ability that cannot legally resolve is a NO-OP that logs, never an error.
   215	  ctx.events.push({ type: 'abilityNoLegalTarget', card: ctx.source, abilityId: ctx.abilityId })
   216	}
   217	
   218	function runEffects(ctx: Ctx, effects: readonly Effect[], depth: number, onSpine: boolean): void {
   219	  const start = onSpine ? (ctx.resume[depth] ?? 0) : 0
   220	  for (let i = start; i < effects.length; i++) {
   221	    const eff = effects[i]
   222	    if (!eff) continue
   223	    ctx.path = [...ctx.path.slice(0, depth), i]
   224	    // Still on the resume spine AND a deeper index was recorded ⇒ this node's choice is already answered:
   225	    // descend into its children rather than raising the same prompt again.
   226	    const answered = onSpine && i === start && depth + 1 < ctx.resume.length
   227	    runEffect(ctx, eff, depth, answered)
   228	    if (ctx.suspend) return
   229	  }
   230	}
   231	
   232	function runEffect(ctx: Ctx, eff: Effect, depth: number, answered: boolean): void {
   233	  step(ctx)
   234	  switch (eff.kind) {
   235	    case 'chooseTargets': {
   236	      if (answered) { runEffects(ctx, eff.then, depth + 1, true); return }
   237	      const candidates = targetCandidates(ctx.state, ctx.source, ctx.controller, eff.from)
   238	      if (candidates.length === 0 || eff.min > candidates.length) { noLegalTarget(ctx); return }
   239	      ctx.suspend = { kind: 'chooseTargets', player: ctx.controller, min: eff.min, max: Math.min(eff.max, candidates.length), candidates }
   240	      return
   241	    }
   242	    case 'chooseModes': {
   243	      if (answered) {
   244	        const from = ctx.resume[depth + 1] ?? 0
   245	        for (let k = from; k < ctx.modes.length; k++) {
   246	          ctx.path = [...ctx.path.slice(0, depth + 1), k]
   247	          const mode = eff.modes[ctx.modes[k] ?? -1]
   248	          if (mode) runEffects(ctx, mode.effects, depth + 2, k === from)
   249	          if (ctx.suspend) return
   250	        }
   251	        return
   252	      }
   253	      if (eff.modes.length === 0 || eff.min > eff.modes.length) { noLegalTarget(ctx); return }
   254	      ctx.suspend = { kind: 'chooseMode', player: ctx.controller, min: eff.min, max: Math.min(eff.max, eff.modes.length), labels: eff.modes.map((m) => m.label) }
   255	      return
   256	    }
   257	    case 'forEach': {
   258	      // Untargeted, so it raises no prompt — and it must not contain one either: `Frame.chosen` is a single
   259	      // innermost binding, so a suspension inside `do` could not restore the per-iteration card on resume.
   260	      const saved = ctx.chosen
   261	      for (const id of targetCandidates(ctx.state, ctx.source, ctx.controller, eff.from)) {
   262	        ctx.chosen = [id]
   263	        runEffects(ctx, eff.do, depth + 1, false)
   264	        if (ctx.suspend) throw new Error(`ability ${ctx.abilityId}: forEach.do must not contain a suspending effect`)
   265	      }
   266	      ctx.chosen = saved
   267	      return
   268	    }
   269	    case 'onSubject': {
   270	      // The card the trigger was ABOUT — Luso's "break it" (spec C2-5). Same fixed-binding shape as
   271	      // `forEach`, so `do` may not suspend: `Frame.chosen` holds one innermost binding and a prompt inside
   272	      // `do` could not restore the subject on resume. A trigger with no card subject is a no-op.
   273	      const ev = ctx.triggerEvent
   274	      const subject = ev === null ? null : ev.kind === 'damage' ? ev.target : ev.card
   275	      if (subject === null) return
   276	      const saved = ctx.chosen
   277	      ctx.chosen = [subject]
   278	      runEffects(ctx, eff.do, depth + 1, false)
   279	      if (ctx.suspend) throw new Error(`ability ${ctx.abilityId}: onSubject.do must not contain a suspending effect`)
   280	      ctx.chosen = saved
   281	      return
   282	    }
   283	    case 'dull':
   284	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   285	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   286	        if (!loc || loc.card.status === 'dull') continue
   287	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, status: 'dull' }))
   288	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'dulled', card: id })
   289	      }
   290	      return
   291	    case 'damage': {
   292	      const hits: DamageOccurrence[] = []
   293	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   294	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   295	        if (!loc || loc.zone !== 'forwards') continue   // only Forwards carry damage
   296	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, damage: c.damage + eff.amount }))
   297	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'abilityDamage', source: ctx.source, target: id, amount: eff.amount })
   298	        hits.push({ source: ctx.source, sourceController: ctx.controller, target: id, victim: null, amount: eff.amount })
   299	      }
   300	      ctx.state = enqueueDamageTriggers(ctx.state, hits)   // ability damage triggers exactly as combat damage does (spec C2-7)
   301	      // §12.4.5 turns this into a break; `settle` runs the rule processes, which honour `cannotBeBroken`. Because
   302	      // `drainResolution` yields between frames (spec C2-6), that process resolves BEFORE the trigger just queued.
   303	      return
   304	    }
   305	    case 'breakCard': {
   306	      // An ability break is a field→Break Zone transition like any other, and Lightning's "when a Forward
   307	      // opponent controls is put from the field into the Break Zone" is cause-agnostic. This path used to do its
   308	      // own zone move and never produce a transition, so NO observer clause fired on an ability break —
   309	      // ~130 of ~220 ability breaks on the shipped gate had an eligible watcher standing, and every test,
   310	      // invariant and fuzzer run was green while it silently missed them.
   311	      const pre = ctx.state   // watchers are read PRE-move, so one that breaks itself here still triggers
   312	      const moved: ZoneTransition[] = []
   313	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   314	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   315	        if (!loc) continue
   316	        if (loc.card.flags.includes('cannotBeBroken')) { ctx.events.push({ type: 'breakPrevented', card: id, flag: 'cannotBeBroken' }); continue }
   317	        // `loc.owner` is the field the card sat on — its CONTROLLER. Real ownership is `CardInstance.owner`, and
   318	        // §12.4.4/§15.1.1.3 sends a broken card to its OWNER's Break Zone. They coincide across the MVP0 pool.
   319	        const owner = ctx.state.cards[id]?.owner ?? loc.owner
   320	        moved.push({
   321	          card: id, controller: loc.owner, owner,
   322	          from: loc.zone === 'backups' ? 'backups' : 'forwards', to: 'breakZone', reason: 'ability',
   323	          cause: ctx.source, causeController: ctx.controller, snapshot: loc.card,
   324	        })
   325	        ctx.state = updatePlayer(removeFromField(ctx.state, id), owner, (ps) => ({ ...ps, breakZone: [...ps.breakZone, id] }))
   326	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'brokenByAbility', card: id, source: ctx.source })
   327	      }
   328	      ctx.state = enqueueZoneChangeTriggers(pre, ctx.state, moved)
   329	      return
   330	    }
   331	    case 'addPower':
   332	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   333	        if (!findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)) continue
   334	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, powerBonus: c.powerBonus + eff.amount }))
   335	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'powerModified', card: id, amount: eff.amount })
   336	      }
   337	      return
   338	    case 'grantKeyword':
   339	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   340	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   341	        if (!loc || loc.card.granted.includes(eff.keyword)) continue
   342	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, granted: [...c.granted, eff.keyword] }))
   343	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'keywordGranted', card: id, keyword: eff.keyword })
   344	      }
   345	      return
   346	    case 'grantFlag':
   347	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   348	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   349	        if (!loc || loc.card.flags.includes(eff.flag)) continue
   350	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, flags: [...c.flags, eff.flag] }))
   351	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'flagGranted', card: id, flag: eff.flag })
   352	      }
   353	      return
   354	    case 'moveToHand':
   355	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   356	        const moved = toHand(ctx.state, id)
   357	        if (!moved) continue
   358	        ctx.state = moved
   359	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'returnedToHand', player: ctx.state.cards[id]?.owner ?? ctx.controller, card: id })
   360	      }
   361	      return
   362	    default: { const _exhaustive: never = eff; return _exhaustive }
   363	  }
   364	}
   365	
   366	interface FrameResult { state: GameState; events: Event[]; pending: Pending | null; frame: Frame; steps: number }
   367	
   368	function runFrame(state: GameState, frame: Frame): FrameResult {
   369	  const ability = abilityOf(state, frame)
   370	  const base: FrameResult = { state, events: [], pending: null, frame, steps: state.resolution.steps }
   371	  if (!ability) return base   // the clause vanished with its def; drop the frame rather than throw
   372	  const ctx: Ctx = {
   373	    state, events: [], source: frame.source, controller: frame.controller, abilityId: frame.abilityId,
   374	    path: [...frame.path], chosen: [...frame.chosen], modes: [...frame.modes],
   375	    triggerEvent: frame.triggerEvent,
   376	    resume: frame.path, suspend: null, steps: state.resolution.steps,
   377	  }
   378	  runEffects(ctx, ability.effects, 0, frame.path.length > 0)
   379	  return {
   380	    state: ctx.state, events: ctx.events, pending: ctx.suspend, steps: ctx.steps,
   381	    frame: { ...frame, path: ctx.path, chosen: ctx.chosen, modes: ctx.modes },
   382	  }
   383	}
   384	
   385	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   386	// Draining
   387	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   388	
   389	/** §10.1.1 Attack Preparation Step, then §10.1.2 Declaration. Shared by `pass` and by the agenda continuation. */
   390	export function enterAttackDeclaration(state: GameState, player: PlayerId): [GameState, Event[]] {
   391	  const s: GameState = { ...state, phase: 'attack', attack: { step: 'declaration', attackers: [], blocker: null }, priority: player }
   392	  return [s, [{ type: 'phaseStarted', phase: 'attack', step: 'preparation' }, { type: 'phaseStarted', phase: 'attack', step: 'declaration' }]]
   393	}
   394	
   395	/**
   396	 * Advance the agenda by exactly ONE frame: resume the active one, or start the next queued one, and run it until
   397	 * it finishes or a player must choose (the choice becomes `state.pending` and the frame stays `active`). Then
   398	 * YIELD — spec C2-6. `settle` in apply.ts owns the loop and runs §12.3 rule processes before the next frame
   399	 * starts, which is what puts §12.4.5's break ahead of the trigger that same damage queued. Draining the whole
   400	 * queue here instead would resolve Luso before the Forward it killed was broken.
   401	 *
   402	 * With the queue and the active frame both empty, the system continuation — if any — runs. Never touches an
   403	 * existing `pending`: the decision already on the table always comes first.
   404	 *
   405	 * `resolution.steps` is NOT reset here: `settle` in apply.ts resets it once the whole settlement is quiet, so a
   406	 * rule-process ⇄ trigger cycle keeps accumulating and hits the cap instead of restarting the count every pass.
   407	 */
   408	export function drainResolution(state: GameState): [GameState, Event[]] {
   409	  const events: Event[] = []
   410	  let s = state
   411	  if (s.result || s.pending) return [s, events]
   412	  let frame = s.resolution.active
   413	  if (!frame) {
   414	    const [next, ...rest] = s.resolution.queue
   415	    if (next) {
   416	      frame = next
   417	      const steps = s.resolution.steps + 1   // starting a frame is a step too, so a cycle of empty clauses is still capped
   418	      if (steps > MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS) throw new Error(`resolution exceeded ${MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS} steps (spec C1-5) — trigger cycle?`)
   419	      s = { ...s, resolution: { ...s.resolution, active: frame, queue: rest, steps } }
   420	      events.push({ type: 'abilityTriggered', player: frame.controller, card: frame.source, abilityId: frame.abilityId })
   421	    }
   422	  }
   423	  if (frame) {
   424	    const r = runFrame(s, frame)
   425	    s = r.state
   426	    events.push(...r.events)
   427	    s = r.pending
   428	      ? { ...s, pending: r.pending, resolution: { ...s.resolution, active: r.frame, steps: r.steps } }
   429	      : { ...s, resolution: { ...s.resolution, active: null, steps: r.steps } }
   430	    return [s, events]   // one frame per call; `settle` comes back with rule processes run
   431	  }
   432	  const continuation = s.resolution.continuation
   433	  if (continuation === 'enterAttackDeclaration') {
   434	    s = { ...s, resolution: { ...s.resolution, continuation: null } }
   435	    const [t, e] = enterAttackDeclaration(s, s.turnPlayer)
   436	    s = t; events.push(...e)
   437	  }
   438	  return [s, events]
   439	}
   440	
   441	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   442	// Answering a suspended choice
   443	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   444	
   445	/**
   446	 * The effect node a frame is suspended at, found by walking `path` through the AST. `apply` re-derives its
   447	 * candidates from HERE rather than trusting `state.pending`, which is only a projection of it (spec C1-6).
   448	 */
   449	function effectAt(effects: readonly Effect[], path: readonly number[], modes: readonly number[], depth: number): Effect | null {
   450	  const i = path[depth]
   451	  if (i === undefined) return null
   452	  const eff = effects[i]
   453	  if (!eff) return null
   454	  if (depth === path.length - 1) return eff
   455	  if (eff.kind === 'chooseTargets') return effectAt(eff.then, path, modes, depth + 1)
   456	  if (eff.kind === 'chooseModes') {
   457	    const k = path[depth + 1]
   458	    if (k === undefined) return null
   459	    const mode = eff.modes[modes[k] ?? -1]
   460	    return mode ? effectAt(mode.effects, path, modes, depth + 2) : null
   461	  }
   462	  return null
   463	}
   464	
   465	function suspendedNode(state: GameState): { frame: Frame; node: Effect } {
   466	  const frame = state.resolution.active
   467	  if (!frame) throw new IllegalCommandError('no ability is waiting for an answer')
   468	  const ability = abilityOf(state, frame)
   469	  if (!ability) throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability no longer exists')
   470	  const node = effectAt(ability.effects, frame.path, frame.modes, 0)
   471	  if (!node) throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability has no effect at its program counter')
   472	  return { frame, node }
   473	}
   474	
   475	export function applyChooseTargets(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, targets: readonly CardId[]): [GameState, Event[]] {
   476	  if (state.pending?.kind !== 'chooseTargets' || state.pending.player !== player) throw new IllegalCommandError('no target choice owed by this player')
   477	  const { frame, node } = suspendedNode(state)
   478	  if (node.kind !== 'chooseTargets') throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability is not choosing targets')
   479	  if (new Set(targets).size !== targets.length) throw new IllegalCommandError('duplicate target')
   480	  const candidates = targetCandidates(state, frame.source, frame.controller, node.from)
   481	  const max = Math.min(node.max, candidates.length)
   482	  if (targets.length < node.min || targets.length > max) throw new IllegalCommandError(`choose ${node.min}..${max} targets, got ${targets.length}`)
   483	  for (const id of targets) if (!candidates.includes(id)) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${id} is not a legal target`)
   484	  // Extending the path by one level says "the choice at this node is made" — resume runs `then`, not the prompt.
   485	  const active: Frame = { ...frame, chosen: [...targets], path: [...frame.path, 0] }
   486	  return [{ ...state, pending: null, resolution: { ...state.resolution, active } }, []]
   487	}
   488	
   489	export function applyChooseMode(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, modes: readonly number[]): [GameState, Event[]] {
   490	  if (state.pending?.kind !== 'chooseMode' || state.pending.player !== player) throw new IllegalCommandError('no mode choice owed by this player')
   491	  const { frame, node } = suspendedNode(state)
   492	  if (node.kind !== 'chooseModes') throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability is not choosing modes')
   493	  if (new Set(modes).size !== modes.length) throw new IllegalCommandError('duplicate mode')
   494	  const max = Math.min(node.max, node.modes.length)
   495	  if (modes.length < node.min || modes.length > max) throw new IllegalCommandError(`choose ${node.min}..${max} modes, got ${modes.length}`)
   496	  for (const m of modes) if (!Number.isInteger(m) || m < 0 || m >= node.modes.length) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${m} is not a mode of this ability`)
   497	  const ordered = [...modes].sort((a, b) => a - b)   // "select up to 2 of the 3 following" resolves in PRINTED order
   498	  const active: Frame = { ...frame, modes: ordered, path: [...frame.path, 0, 0] }
   499	  return [{ ...state, pending: null, resolution: { ...state.resolution, active } }, []]
   500	}
   501	
   502	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   503	// Zone-change watcher dispatch (spec C2-3/C2-4). Lives here, not in rules.ts, because rules.ts already imports
   504	// this module — keeping dispatch in one place avoids a runtime import cycle.
   505	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   506	/**
   507	 * One trigger occurrence: a (watcher, clause, matching transition) TRIPLE (spec C2-3). CR §11.8.6 — a Lightning
   508	 * watching two opponent Forwards broken at the same instant triggers TWICE, so this is deliberately not
   509	 * collapsed to one occurrence per batch.
   510	 */
   511	interface WatcherOccurrence {
   512	  readonly transition: ZoneTransition
   513	  readonly source: CardId

   118	  if (filter.types !== undefined && !filter.types.includes(def.type)) return false
   119	  if (filter.element !== undefined && !def.elements.includes(filter.element)) return false
   120	  if (filter.maxCost !== undefined && def.cost > filter.maxCost) return false
   121	  if (filter.excludeSource && id === source) return false
   122	  if (filter.excludeSourceName) {
   123	    const src = defFor(state, source)
   124	    if (src && src.name === def.name) return false
   125	  }
   126	  return true
   127	}
   128	
   129	/**
   130	 * The legal targets of one `TargetSpec`, in a fixed player-0-then-1 order so a live state and its
   131	 * determinisation enumerate the same candidates in the same order (spec C1-A6).
   132	 */
   133	export function targetCandidates(state: GameState, source: CardId, controller: PlayerId, spec: TargetSpec): CardId[] {
   134	  const owners: readonly PlayerId[] = spec.controller === 'any' ? [0, 1]
   135	    : spec.controller === 'self' ? [controller] : [opponentOf(controller)]
   136	  const out: CardId[] = []
   137	  for (const p of ([0, 1] as const).filter((q) => owners.includes(q))) {
   138	    const ps = state.players[p]
   139	    const ids = spec.zone === 'breakZone' ? ps.breakZone
   140	      : (spec.zone === 'forwards' ? ps.forwards : ps.backups).map((c) => c.id)
   141	    for (const id of ids) if (matchesFilter(state, source, id, spec.filter)) out.push(id)
   142	  }
   143	  return out
   144	}
   145	
   146	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   147	// Zone plumbing
   148	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   149	
   150	function setFieldCard(state: GameState, id: CardId, f: (c: FieldCard) => FieldCard): GameState {
   151	  const loc = findFieldCard(state, id)
   152	  if (!loc) return state
   153	  return updatePlayer(state, loc.owner, (ps) => (loc.zone === 'forwards'
   154	    ? { ...ps, forwards: ps.forwards.map((c) => (c.id === id ? f(c) : c)) }
   155	    : { ...ps, backups: ps.backups.map((c) => (c.id === id ? f(c) : c))}))
   156	}
   157	
   158	function removeFromField(state: GameState, id: CardId): GameState {
   159	  const loc = findFieldCard(state, id)
   160	  if (!loc) return state
   161	  return updatePlayer(state, loc.owner, (ps) => (loc.zone === 'forwards'
   162	    ? { ...ps, forwards: ps.forwards.filter((c) => c.id !== id) }
   163	    : { ...ps, backups: ps.backups.filter((c) => c.id !== id) }))
   164	}
   165	
   166	/** §7.10: a card always goes to its OWNER's zone, not its controller's. Returns null if the card is nowhere movable. */
   167	function toHand(state: GameState, id: CardId): GameState | null {
   168	  const owner = state.cards[id]?.owner
   169	  if (owner === undefined) return null
   170	  let s = state
   171	  if (findFieldCard(state, id)) s = removeFromField(s, id)
   172	  else {
   173	    const holder = ([0, 1] as const).find((p) => state.players[p].breakZone.includes(id))
   174	    if (holder === undefined) return null
   175	    s = updatePlayer(s, holder, (ps) => ({ ...ps, breakZone: ps.breakZone.filter((x) => x !== id) }))
   176	  }
   177	  return updatePlayer(s, owner, (ps) => ({ ...ps, hand: [...ps.hand, id] }))
   178	}
   179	
   180	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   181	// The walker
   182	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   183	
   184	interface Ctx {
   185	  state: GameState
   186	  events: Event[]
   187	  source: CardId
   188	  controller: PlayerId
   189	  abilityId: string
   190	  /** Program counter, one index per nesting level. `chooseModes` owns TWO levels: mode ordinal, then effect index. */
   191	  path: number[]
   192	  chosen: CardId[]
   193	  modes: number[]
   194	  /** What fired this clause, for `onSubject` and narration; null for self-triggers (spec C2-5). */
   195	  triggerEvent: TriggerEvent | null
   196	  /** The path the frame was suspended at; execution rejoins it instead of replaying the effects already run. */
   197	  resume: readonly number[]
   198	  suspend: Pending | null
   199	  steps: number
   200	}
   201	
   202	/**
   203	 * Spec C1-5: every effect step is counted, the count lives on `GameState` and therefore PERSISTS across player
   204	 * choices. A call-depth cap would not see a trigger cycle that launders itself through a `chooseTargets` prompt.
   205	 */
   206	function step(ctx: Ctx): void {
   207	  ctx.steps++
   208	  if (ctx.steps > MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS) {
   209	    throw new Error(`ability ${ctx.abilityId} on card ${ctx.source} exceeded ${MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS} resolution steps (spec C1-5) — trigger cycle?`)
   210	  }
   211	}
   212	
   213	function noLegalTarget(ctx: Ctx): void {
   214	  // Spec C1-7: an ability that cannot legally resolve is a NO-OP that logs, never an error.
   215	  ctx.events.push({ type: 'abilityNoLegalTarget', card: ctx.source, abilityId: ctx.abilityId })
   216	}
   217	
   218	function runEffects(ctx: Ctx, effects: readonly Effect[], depth: number, onSpine: boolean): void {
   219	  const start = onSpine ? (ctx.resume[depth] ?? 0) : 0
   220	  for (let i = start; i < effects.length; i++) {
   221	    const eff = effects[i]
   222	    if (!eff) continue
   223	    ctx.path = [...ctx.path.slice(0, depth), i]
   224	    // Still on the resume spine AND a deeper index was recorded ⇒ this node's choice is already answered:
   225	    // descend into its children rather than raising the same prompt again.
   226	    const answered = onSpine && i === start && depth + 1 < ctx.resume.length
   227	    runEffect(ctx, eff, depth, answered)
   228	    if (ctx.suspend) return
   229	  }
   230	}
   231	
   232	function runEffect(ctx: Ctx, eff: Effect, depth: number, answered: boolean): void {
   233	  step(ctx)
   234	  switch (eff.kind) {
   235	    case 'chooseTargets': {
   236	      if (answered) { runEffects(ctx, eff.then, depth + 1, true); return }
   237	      const candidates = targetCandidates(ctx.state, ctx.source, ctx.controller, eff.from)
   238	      if (candidates.length === 0 || eff.min > candidates.length) { noLegalTarget(ctx); return }
   239	      ctx.suspend = { kind: 'chooseTargets', player: ctx.controller, min: eff.min, max: Math.min(eff.max, candidates.length), candidates }
   240	      return
   241	    }
   242	    case 'chooseModes': {
   243	      if (answered) {
   244	        const from = ctx.resume[depth + 1] ?? 0
   245	        for (let k = from; k < ctx.modes.length; k++) {
   246	          ctx.path = [...ctx.path.slice(0, depth + 1), k]
   247	          const mode = eff.modes[ctx.modes[k] ?? -1]
   248	          if (mode) runEffects(ctx, mode.effects, depth + 2, k === from)
   249	          if (ctx.suspend) return
   250	        }
   251	        return
   252	      }
   253	      if (eff.modes.length === 0 || eff.min > eff.modes.length) { noLegalTarget(ctx); return }
   254	      ctx.suspend = { kind: 'chooseMode', player: ctx.controller, min: eff.min, max: Math.min(eff.max, eff.modes.length), labels: eff.modes.map((m) => m.label) }
   255	      return
   256	    }
   257	    case 'forEach': {
   258	      // Untargeted, so it raises no prompt — and it must not contain one either: `Frame.chosen` is a single
   259	      // innermost binding, so a suspension inside `do` could not restore the per-iteration card on resume.
   260	      const saved = ctx.chosen
   261	      for (const id of targetCandidates(ctx.state, ctx.source, ctx.controller, eff.from)) {
   262	        ctx.chosen = [id]
   263	        runEffects(ctx, eff.do, depth + 1, false)
   264	        if (ctx.suspend) throw new Error(`ability ${ctx.abilityId}: forEach.do must not contain a suspending effect`)
   265	      }
   266	      ctx.chosen = saved
   267	      return
   268	    }
   269	    case 'onSubject': {
   270	      // The card the trigger was ABOUT — Luso's "break it" (spec C2-5). Same fixed-binding shape as
   271	      // `forEach`, so `do` may not suspend: `Frame.chosen` holds one innermost binding and a prompt inside
   272	      // `do` could not restore the subject on resume. A trigger with no card subject is a no-op.
   273	      const ev = ctx.triggerEvent
   274	      const subject = ev === null ? null : ev.kind === 'damage' ? ev.target : ev.card
   275	      if (subject === null) return
   276	      const saved = ctx.chosen
   277	      ctx.chosen = [subject]
   278	      runEffects(ctx, eff.do, depth + 1, false)
   279	      if (ctx.suspend) throw new Error(`ability ${ctx.abilityId}: onSubject.do must not contain a suspending effect`)
   280	      ctx.chosen = saved
   281	      return
   282	    }
   283	    case 'dull':
   284	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   285	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   286	        if (!loc || loc.card.status === 'dull') continue
   287	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, status: 'dull' }))
   288	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'dulled', card: id })
   289	      }
   290	      return
   291	    case 'damage': {
   292	      const hits: DamageOccurrence[] = []
   293	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   294	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   295	        if (!loc || loc.zone !== 'forwards') continue   // only Forwards carry damage
   296	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, damage: c.damage + eff.amount }))
   297	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'abilityDamage', source: ctx.source, target: id, amount: eff.amount })
   298	        hits.push({ source: ctx.source, sourceController: ctx.controller, target: id, victim: null, amount: eff.amount })
   299	      }
   300	      ctx.state = enqueueDamageTriggers(ctx.state, hits)   // ability damage triggers exactly as combat damage does (spec C2-7)
   301	      // §12.4.5 turns this into a break; `settle` runs the rule processes, which honour `cannotBeBroken`. Because
   302	      // `drainResolution` yields between frames (spec C2-6), that process resolves BEFORE the trigger just queued.
   303	      return
   304	    }
   305	    case 'breakCard': {
   306	      // An ability break is a field→Break Zone transition like any other, and Lightning's "when a Forward
   307	      // opponent controls is put from the field into the Break Zone" is cause-agnostic. This path used to do its
   308	      // own zone move and never produce a transition, so NO observer clause fired on an ability break —
   309	      // ~130 of ~220 ability breaks on the shipped gate had an eligible watcher standing, and every test,
   310	      // invariant and fuzzer run was green while it silently missed them.
   311	      const pre = ctx.state   // watchers are read PRE-move, so one that breaks itself here still triggers
   312	      const moved: ZoneTransition[] = []
   313	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   314	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   315	        if (!loc) continue
   316	        if (loc.card.flags.includes('cannotBeBroken')) { ctx.events.push({ type: 'breakPrevented', card: id, flag: 'cannotBeBroken' }); continue }
   317	        // `loc.owner` is the field the card sat on — its CONTROLLER. Real ownership is `CardInstance.owner`, and
   318	        // §12.4.4/§15.1.1.3 sends a broken card to its OWNER's Break Zone. They coincide across the MVP0 pool.
   319	        const owner = ctx.state.cards[id]?.owner ?? loc.owner
   320	        moved.push({
   321	          card: id, controller: loc.owner, owner,
   322	          from: loc.zone === 'backups' ? 'backups' : 'forwards', to: 'breakZone', reason: 'ability',
   323	          cause: ctx.source, causeController: ctx.controller, snapshot: loc.card,
   324	        })
   325	        ctx.state = updatePlayer(removeFromField(ctx.state, id), owner, (ps) => ({ ...ps, breakZone: [...ps.breakZone, id] }))
   326	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'brokenByAbility', card: id, source: ctx.source })
   327	      }
   328	      ctx.state = enqueueZoneChangeTriggers(pre, ctx.state, moved)
   329	      return
   330	    }
   331	    case 'addPower':
   332	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   333	        if (!findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)) continue
   334	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, powerBonus: c.powerBonus + eff.amount }))
   335	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'powerModified', card: id, amount: eff.amount })
   336	      }
   337	      return
   338	    case 'grantKeyword':
   339	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   340	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   341	        if (!loc || loc.card.granted.includes(eff.keyword)) continue
   342	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, granted: [...c.granted, eff.keyword] }))
   343	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'keywordGranted', card: id, keyword: eff.keyword })
   344	      }
   345	      return
   346	    case 'grantFlag':
   347	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   348	        const loc = findFieldCard(ctx.state, id)
   349	        if (!loc || loc.card.flags.includes(eff.flag)) continue
   350	        ctx.state = setFieldCard(ctx.state, id, (c) => ({ ...c, flags: [...c.flags, eff.flag] }))
   351	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'flagGranted', card: id, flag: eff.flag })
   352	      }
   353	      return
   354	    case 'moveToHand':
   355	      for (const id of ctx.chosen) {
   356	        const moved = toHand(ctx.state, id)
   357	        if (!moved) continue
   358	        ctx.state = moved
   359	        ctx.events.push({ type: 'returnedToHand', player: ctx.state.cards[id]?.owner ?? ctx.controller, card: id })
   360	      }
   361	      return
   362	    default: { const _exhaustive: never = eff; return _exhaustive }
   363	  }
   364	}
   365	
   366	interface FrameResult { state: GameState; events: Event[]; pending: Pending | null; frame: Frame; steps: number }
   367	
   368	function runFrame(state: GameState, frame: Frame): FrameResult {
   369	  const ability = abilityOf(state, frame)
   370	  const base: FrameResult = { state, events: [], pending: null, frame, steps: state.resolution.steps }
   371	  if (!ability) return base   // the clause vanished with its def; drop the frame rather than throw
   372	  const ctx: Ctx = {
   373	    state, events: [], source: frame.source, controller: frame.controller, abilityId: frame.abilityId,
   374	    path: [...frame.path], chosen: [...frame.chosen], modes: [...frame.modes],
   375	    triggerEvent: frame.triggerEvent,
   376	    resume: frame.path, suspend: null, steps: state.resolution.steps,
   377	  }
   378	  runEffects(ctx, ability.effects, 0, frame.path.length > 0)
   379	  return {
   380	    state: ctx.state, events: ctx.events, pending: ctx.suspend, steps: ctx.steps,
   381	    frame: { ...frame, path: ctx.path, chosen: ctx.chosen, modes: ctx.modes },
   382	  }
   383	}
   384	
   385	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   386	// Draining
   387	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   388	
   389	/** §10.1.1 Attack Preparation Step, then §10.1.2 Declaration. Shared by `pass` and by the agenda continuation. */
   390	export function enterAttackDeclaration(state: GameState, player: PlayerId): [GameState, Event[]] {
   391	  const s: GameState = { ...state, phase: 'attack', attack: { step: 'declaration', attackers: [], blocker: null }, priority: player }
   392	  return [s, [{ type: 'phaseStarted', phase: 'attack', step: 'preparation' }, { type: 'phaseStarted', phase: 'attack', step: 'declaration' }]]
   393	}
   394	
   395	/**
   396	 * Advance the agenda by exactly ONE frame: resume the active one, or start the next queued one, and run it until
   397	 * it finishes or a player must choose (the choice becomes `state.pending` and the frame stays `active`). Then
   398	 * YIELD — spec C2-6. `settle` in apply.ts owns the loop and runs §12.3 rule processes before the next frame
   399	 * starts, which is what puts §12.4.5's break ahead of the trigger that same damage queued. Draining the whole
   400	 * queue here instead would resolve Luso before the Forward it killed was broken.
   401	 *
   402	 * With the queue and the active frame both empty, the system continuation — if any — runs. Never touches an
   403	 * existing `pending`: the decision already on the table always comes first.
   404	 *
   405	 * `resolution.steps` is NOT reset here: `settle` in apply.ts resets it once the whole settlement is quiet, so a
   406	 * rule-process ⇄ trigger cycle keeps accumulating and hits the cap instead of restarting the count every pass.
   407	 */
   408	export function drainResolution(state: GameState): [GameState, Event[]] {
   409	  const events: Event[] = []
   410	  let s = state
   411	  if (s.result || s.pending) return [s, events]
   412	  let frame = s.resolution.active
   413	  if (!frame) {
   414	    const [next, ...rest] = s.resolution.queue
   415	    if (next) {
   416	      frame = next
   417	      const steps = s.resolution.steps + 1   // starting a frame is a step too, so a cycle of empty clauses is still capped
   418	      if (steps > MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS) throw new Error(`resolution exceeded ${MAX_RESOLUTION_STEPS} steps (spec C1-5) — trigger cycle?`)
   419	      s = { ...s, resolution: { ...s.resolution, active: frame, queue: rest, steps } }
   420	      events.push({ type: 'abilityTriggered', player: frame.controller, card: frame.source, abilityId: frame.abilityId })
   421	    }
   422	  }
   423	  if (frame) {
   424	    const r = runFrame(s, frame)
   425	    s = r.state
   426	    events.push(...r.events)
   427	    s = r.pending
   428	      ? { ...s, pending: r.pending, resolution: { ...s.resolution, active: r.frame, steps: r.steps } }
   429	      : { ...s, resolution: { ...s.resolution, active: null, steps: r.steps } }
   430	    return [s, events]   // one frame per call; `settle` comes back with rule processes run
   431	  }
   432	  const continuation = s.resolution.continuation
   433	  if (continuation === 'enterAttackDeclaration') {
   434	    s = { ...s, resolution: { ...s.resolution, continuation: null } }
   435	    const [t, e] = enterAttackDeclaration(s, s.turnPlayer)
   436	    s = t; events.push(...e)
   437	  }
   438	  return [s, events]
   439	}
   440	
   441	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   442	// Answering a suspended choice
   443	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   444	
   445	/**
   446	 * The effect node a frame is suspended at, found by walking `path` through the AST. `apply` re-derives its
   447	 * candidates from HERE rather than trusting `state.pending`, which is only a projection of it (spec C1-6).
   448	 */
   449	function effectAt(effects: readonly Effect[], path: readonly number[], modes: readonly number[], depth: number): Effect | null {
   450	  const i = path[depth]
   451	  if (i === undefined) return null
   452	  const eff = effects[i]
   453	  if (!eff) return null
   454	  if (depth === path.length - 1) return eff
   455	  if (eff.kind === 'chooseTargets') return effectAt(eff.then, path, modes, depth + 1)
   456	  if (eff.kind === 'chooseModes') {
   457	    const k = path[depth + 1]
   458	    if (k === undefined) return null
   459	    const mode = eff.modes[modes[k] ?? -1]
   460	    return mode ? effectAt(mode.effects, path, modes, depth + 2) : null
   461	  }
   462	  return null
   463	}
   464	
   465	function suspendedNode(state: GameState): { frame: Frame; node: Effect } {
   466	  const frame = state.resolution.active
   467	  if (!frame) throw new IllegalCommandError('no ability is waiting for an answer')
   468	  const ability = abilityOf(state, frame)
   469	  if (!ability) throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability no longer exists')
   470	  const node = effectAt(ability.effects, frame.path, frame.modes, 0)
   471	  if (!node) throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability has no effect at its program counter')
   472	  return { frame, node }
   473	}
   474	
   475	export function applyChooseTargets(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, targets: readonly CardId[]): [GameState, Event[]] {
   476	  if (state.pending?.kind !== 'chooseTargets' || state.pending.player !== player) throw new IllegalCommandError('no target choice owed by this player')
   477	  const { frame, node } = suspendedNode(state)
   478	  if (node.kind !== 'chooseTargets') throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability is not choosing targets')
   479	  if (new Set(targets).size !== targets.length) throw new IllegalCommandError('duplicate target')
   480	  const candidates = targetCandidates(state, frame.source, frame.controller, node.from)
   481	  const max = Math.min(node.max, candidates.length)
   482	  if (targets.length < node.min || targets.length > max) throw new IllegalCommandError(`choose ${node.min}..${max} targets, got ${targets.length}`)
   483	  for (const id of targets) if (!candidates.includes(id)) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${id} is not a legal target`)
   484	  // Extending the path by one level says "the choice at this node is made" — resume runs `then`, not the prompt.
   485	  const active: Frame = { ...frame, chosen: [...targets], path: [...frame.path, 0] }
   486	  return [{ ...state, pending: null, resolution: { ...state.resolution, active } }, []]
   487	}
   488	
   489	export function applyChooseMode(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, modes: readonly number[]): [GameState, Event[]] {
   490	  if (state.pending?.kind !== 'chooseMode' || state.pending.player !== player) throw new IllegalCommandError('no mode choice owed by this player')
   491	  const { frame, node } = suspendedNode(state)
   492	  if (node.kind !== 'chooseModes') throw new IllegalCommandError('the waiting ability is not choosing modes')
   493	  if (new Set(modes).size !== modes.length) throw new IllegalCommandError('duplicate mode')
   494	  const max = Math.min(node.max, node.modes.length)
   495	  if (modes.length < node.min || modes.length > max) throw new IllegalCommandError(`choose ${node.min}..${max} modes, got ${modes.length}`)
   496	  for (const m of modes) if (!Number.isInteger(m) || m < 0 || m >= node.modes.length) throw new IllegalCommandError(`${m} is not a mode of this ability`)
   497	  const ordered = [...modes].sort((a, b) => a - b)   // "select up to 2 of the 3 following" resolves in PRINTED order
   498	  const active: Frame = { ...frame, modes: ordered, path: [...frame.path, 0, 0] }
   499	  return [{ ...state, pending: null, resolution: { ...state.resolution, active } }, []]
   500	}
   501	
   502	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   503	// Zone-change watcher dispatch (spec C2-3/C2-4). Lives here, not in rules.ts, because rules.ts already imports
   504	// this module — keeping dispatch in one place avoids a runtime import cycle.
   505	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   506	/**
   507	 * One trigger occurrence: a (watcher, clause, matching transition) TRIPLE (spec C2-3). CR §11.8.6 — a Lightning
   508	 * watching two opponent Forwards broken at the same instant triggers TWICE, so this is deliberately not
   509	 * collapsed to one occurrence per batch.
   510	 */
   511	interface WatcherOccurrence {
   512	  readonly transition: ZoneTransition
   513	  readonly source: CardId
   514	  readonly controller: PlayerId
   515	  readonly ability: Ability
   516	}
   517	
   518	/** "Opponent controls" is relative to the WATCHER's controller, never the turn player (spec C2-10). */
   519	function watches(state: GameState, trigger: AbilityTrigger, watcher: PlayerId, t: ZoneTransition): boolean {
   520	  if (trigger.kind !== 'observesZoneChange') return false
   521	  if (trigger.to !== 'breakZone') return false   // `from: 'field'` covers both field arrays
   522	  // The moved card's TYPE, from its def — Lightning watches "a FORWARD … put into the Break Zone". Checking the
   523	  // transition's `from` array instead would be the same implicit restriction that made this safe only by accident.
   524	  const code = state.cards[t.card]?.code
   525	  if ((code === undefined ? undefined : state.defs[code])?.type !== trigger.of) return false
   526	  if (trigger.whose === 'self') return t.controller === watcher
   527	  if (trigger.whose === 'opponent') return t.controller === opponentOf(watcher)
   528	  return true
   529	}
   530	
   531	/**
   532	 * Snapshot the watchers of a whole simultaneous batch BEFORE any of it moves (spec C2-4). A Lightning broken in
   533	 * the SAME batch as its own victim must still trigger, and once removal has run its clause is no longer
   534	 * discoverable from the field at all; `Frame.source` already tolerates an off-field source (C1).
   535	 *
   536	 * Order is spec C2-11's total key — (occurrence index, AP/NAP controller, source zone, pre-event field index,
   537	 * ability index, source id) — produced by CONSTRUCTION rather than by sorting: transitions in batch order, then
   538	 * active before non-active player, then forwards before backups, then field-array index, then printed clause

   266	function chooseModeCandidates(state: GameState, player: PlayerId, pending: Extract<Pending, { kind: 'chooseMode' }>): Command[] {

   268	  const node = suspendedEffect(state)
   269	  if (!frame || node?.kind !== 'chooseModes') return legalCommands(state, player).filter((c) => c.type === 'chooseMode')
   270	  const { ranked, scores } = rankBy(node.modes.map((_, i) => i), (i) => effectsValue(state, player, frame.source, frame.controller, node.modes[i]?.effects ?? []))
   271	  const picks = policyChoices(ranked, scores, pending.min, Math.min(pending.max, ranked.length))

   275	export function candidateCommands(state: GameState, player: PlayerId): Command[] {
   276	  if (state.result || actingPlayer(state) !== player) return []
   277	  const out: Command[] = []
   278	  const pending = state.pending
   279	  if (pending) {
   280	    switch (pending.kind) {

   283	      case 'discardToHandSize': {
   284	        const byValue = [...state.players[player].hand].sort((a, b) => cardValue(defOf(state, a)) - cardValue(defOf(state, b)))

   286	      }
   287	      case 'declareBlock': return [{ type: 'declareBlock', player, blocker: null }, ...legalBlockers(state, player).map((blocker) => ({ type: 'declareBlock' as const, player, blocker }))]
   288	      case 'assignPartyDamage': return legalPartyDamageAssignments(state).map((assignments) => ({ type: 'assignPartyDamage' as const, player, assignments }))

   296	    for (const card of state.players[player].hand) {
   297	      if (castCheck(state, player, card) !== null) continue
   298	      const payment = preferredPayment(state, player, card)
   299	      if (!payment) continue
   300	      out.push({ type: defOf(state, card).type === 'summon' ? 'castSummon' : 'castCharacter', player, card, payment })
   301	    }
   302	    out.push({ type: 'pass', player })

   304	    for (const attackers of boundedAttackSets(state, player)) out.push({ type: 'declareAttack', player, attackers })
   305	    out.push({ type: 'pass', player })
   306	  }

   202	export class GreedyAgent implements Agent {
   203	  private rng: Rng
   204	  private readonly decks: [string[], string[]]
   205	  private readonly depth: 0 | 1 | 2
   206	  private readonly weights: Weights
   207	  private readonly aggression: number
   208	  private readonly maxSimulations: number

   215	  constructor(opts: GreedyOptions) {

   217	    this.weights = opts.weights ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS; this.aggression = opts.aggression ?? 0.5; this.maxSimulations = opts.maxSimulations ?? 2000
   218	  }
   219	  decide(view: PlayerView, legal: Command[]): Command {
   220	    this.lastSimulations = 0; this.lastCandidates = 0; this.lastDepth = 0; this.lastScores = []
   221	    const me = view.me
   222	    const [det, rng] = determinise({ view, decks: this.decks, rng: this.rng })

   108	export function Board({ game }: { game: GameApi }): JSX.Element {

   125	  // most-reachable button on the strip all game. Sort it to the end; nothing else changes order.

   130	  // rarely a click target — which also buys the vertical room two full-size field rows per side would not fit in.
   131	  const field = (p: PlayerId, kind: 'forwards' | 'backups'): JSX.Element[] =>
   132	    view.fields[p][kind].map((c) => (
   133	      <FieldCardView key={c.id} v={view} c={c} choices={choices.byCard.get(c.id) ?? []} selected={selected === c.id} onPick={pick} size={kind === 'backups' ? 'small' : 'field'} />
   134	    ))
   135	
   136	  // Every clickable choice must be reachable, or the game dead-ends: Billy Bob's ETB targets your BREAK ZONE,

   149	        cost={d?.cost ?? 0}
   150	        elements={d?.elements ?? []}
   151	        type={d?.type ?? 'forward'}
   152	        power={d?.power ?? null}

   154	        selected={selected === id}
   155	        size="small"
   156	        onClick={() => pick(id)}
   157	      />
   158	    )
   159	  })
   160	
   161	  return (
   162	    <div className="table">
   163	      <section className="table__seat table__seat--opponent">
   164	        <Seat v={view} p={AI} active={view.priority === AI || view.pending?.player === AI} />
   165	        <Zone label="AI Backups" compact empty={!view.fields[AI].backups.length}>{field(AI, 'backups')}</Zone>
   166	        <Zone label="AI Forwards" empty={!view.fields[AI].forwards.length}>{field(AI, 'forwards')}</Zone>
   167	      </section>
   168	
   169	      <PromptStrip view={view} choices={choices} shown={shown} aiThinking={aiThinking} onChoose={(c) => { setSelected(null); choose(c) }} />
   170	
   171	      {/* `.table__seat--player` is column-reverse, so this list reads bottom-up on screen: the status bar sits
   172	          at the outer edge and forwards end up nearest the prompt strip, meeting the AI's across it. */}
   173	      <section className="table__seat table__seat--player">
   174	        <Seat v={view} p={HUMAN} active={view.priority === HUMAN || view.pending?.player === HUMAN} />
   175	        <Zone label="Your Backups" compact empty={!view.fields[HUMAN].backups.length}>{field(HUMAN, 'backups')}</Zone>
   176	        <Zone label="Your Forwards" empty={!view.fields[HUMAN].forwards.length}>{field(HUMAN, 'forwards')}</Zone>
   177	      </section>
   178	
   179	      <section className="table__hand">
   180	        {orphanCards.length > 0 && <Zone label="Choose a card" compact empty={false}>{orphanCards}</Zone>}
   181	        <div className="hand">
   182	          {view.hand.map((id) => {
   183	            const d = defOf(view, id)
   184	            const forCard = choices.byCard.get(id) ?? []

   188	                code={d?.code ?? '?'}
   189	                name={d?.name ?? 'Unknown'}
   190	                cost={d?.cost ?? 0}
   191	                elements={d?.elements ?? []}
   192	                type={d?.type ?? 'forward'}
   193	                power={d?.power ?? null}
   194	                selectable={forCard.length > 0}
