   275	export function candidateCommands(state: GameState, player: PlayerId): Command[] {
   276	  if (state.result || actingPlayer(state) !== player) return []
   277	  const out: Command[] = []

   281	      case 'chooseFirst': return [{ type: 'chooseFirst', player, goFirst: true }, { type: 'chooseFirst', player, goFirst: false }]
   282	      case 'mulligan': return [{ type: 'mulligan', player, redraw: false }, { type: 'mulligan', player, redraw: true }]
   283	      case 'discardToHandSize': {
   284	        const byValue = [...state.players[player].hand].sort((a, b) => cardValue(defOf(state, a)) - cardValue(defOf(state, b)))
   285	        return [{ type: 'discardToHandSize', player, cards: byValue.slice(0, pending.count) }]
   286	      }
   287	      case 'declareBlock': return [{ type: 'declareBlock', player, blocker: null }, ...legalBlockers(state, player).map((blocker) => ({ type: 'declareBlock' as const, player, blocker }))]
   288	      case 'assignPartyDamage': return legalPartyDamageAssignments(state).map((assignments) => ({ type: 'assignPartyDamage' as const, player, assignments }))
   289	      case 'chooseTargets': return chooseTargetsCandidates(state, player, pending)
   290	      case 'chooseMode': return chooseModeCandidates(state, player, pending)
   291	      // W3: exhaustive — a new Pending kind must fail to compile here rather than silently falling through to phase generation.
   292	      default: { const _exhaustive: never = pending; return _exhaustive }
   293	    }
   294	  }
   295	  if (state.phase === 'main1' || state.phase === 'main2') {
   296	    for (const card of state.players[player].hand) {
   297	      if (castCheck(state, player, card) !== null) continue
   298	      const payment = preferredPayment(state, player, card)
   299	      if (!payment) continue
   300	      out.push({ type: defOf(state, card).type === 'summon' ? 'castSummon' : 'castCharacter', player, card, payment })
   301	    }
   302	    out.push({ type: 'pass', player })
   303	  } else if (state.phase === 'attack' && state.attack?.step === 'declaration') {

   305	    out.push({ type: 'pass', player })

   202	export class GreedyAgent implements Agent {

   205	  private readonly depth: 0 | 1 | 2

   207	  private readonly aggression: number
   208	  private readonly maxSimulations: number

   215	  constructor(opts: GreedyOptions) {
   216	    this.rng = seedRng(opts.seed); this.decks = opts.decks; this.depth = opts.depth ?? 1

   103	export function evaluate(state: GameState, me: PlayerId, weights: Weights = DEFAULT_WEIGHTS, aggression = 0.5): number {

   108	  const theirs = material(state, opp, weights) * 2 * aggression
   109	  return mine - theirs

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d1-ismcts.codex-code-review.md:11:**Search still depends on semantically meaningless hand ordering through incomplete comparators.** `observationKey` declares the hand a multiset (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:461`), but determinisation preserves the root hand order (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:44`). Hand-size discard sorts only by `cardValue` (`packages/ai/src/candidates.ts:284`), while payment selection has cost-only tie comparators (`packages/ai/src/payment.ts:21`, `:75`, `:103`). Reordering an otherwise identical hand can therefore change the sole offered discard or preferred payment; sorting action keys cannot recover an action already pruned away. **Fix:** Use total semantic comparators—value/cost, source kind, card code, element, then canonical public ref—and test searches from hand-order permutations for identical commands and diagnostics.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-heuristic-ai-design.md:38:- **A4**: the built signature is `preferredPayment(state, player, card)` — it operates on a full (determinised) `GameState`, not a bare `PlayerView`, because it needs backup/hand card definitions and `canPay`/`generateCp` from the engine. It also resolves multi-element costs via `requiredElements(def)` (§11.2.1.1 Light/Dark exemption, C3) and bounded backtracking over the required elements (C2, final fix wave) — not simply "dull backups then discard" in element order, and not a single scarcity-first greedy pass either: a single pass, even scarcest-element-first, can still strand a later element when the cheapest per-element pick spends a source only that element's rescue depended on (Codex's 3-element counterexample). Backtracking explores every source-to-element assignment and keeps the cheapest complete one.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-heuristic-ai-design.md:100:- Depth-2 rollouts multiply cost: gated by `maxSimulations`.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-heuristic-ai-design.md:129:`msPerDecision` is **end-to-end**: it wraps `viewFor` (build the player's view), `legalCommands` (skipped for greedy seats — see below), and `agent.decide`, timed per decision in `apps/cli/src/selfplay.ts`. `Agent.needsLegalCommands` is `false` for `GreedyAgent`, so `selfPlay` passes it `legal: []` and never pays for `legalCommands(state, p)` on the greedy hot path; `RandomAgent.needsLegalCommands` is `true` (the default), so its `msPerDecision` figures below *do* include a full `legalCommands` call. This asymmetry is why greedy's per-decision cost (~0.2–0.4 ms, dominated by determinise + rollout) is not directly comparable to random's (~0.05 ms, dominated by `legalCommands`'s payment enumeration) as a measure of "who does more work" — they are timing different things.
docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-26-heuristic-ai-design.md:158:**Re-verified again after the fix wave's own re-review (2026-08-27, `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS` unchanged, depth 1, same `--seed 1` gate)**: greedy(p0) vs random **200/0** (100 %); random vs greedy(p1) **2/198** (99 %). All 200/200 completed, 0 failures; 0.27 / 0.28 ms per greedy decision. Both seats improved by one game over the row above — the re-review's R1 fix (`preferredPayment` ranks required-element sources by card value again, not by CP generated) stops the agent discarding a high-power forward where a cost-1 summon would pay the same cost, so it is a small genuine strength gain rather than seed noise. But C2 explicitly deduplicates per batch (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c2-observer-triggers.md:26`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c2-observer-triggers.md:57`). Lightning must trigger once for every matching Forward moved, so two opponent Forwards in one batch produce two triggers, per [CR 3.3 §11.8.6](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf).
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-c2-observer-triggers.codex-review.md:53:Also, AP-first FIFO is deterministic but not “§12.3-ish”: CR 3.3 §11.8.7 lets each controller order their simultaneous triggers and places the non-turn player’s triggers on top. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-rung-a-heuristic-ai.codex-review.md:17:- **HIGH — `preferredPayment` can return `null` for an affordable multi-element cast.** [`plan:491–495`](/Users/danielroach/repos/fftcg-game/.claude/worktrees/rung-a-heuristic-ai/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-rung-a-heuristic-ai.md:491) greedily assigns the cheapest flexible source to the first required element. Example: an Earth/Lightning cost-3 target, a cheap dual-element discard, and an expensive Earth-only discard. The algorithm spends the dual card as Earth, then cannot satisfy Lightning; spending Earth-only as Earth and dual as Lightning is legal. **Change:** assign scarce elements first or perform bounded backtracking across required elements, then greedily fill generic CP; add this counterexample as a test.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.codex-review.md:23:Only Shantotto and Billy Bob are wholly within the stated slice. Noel also has EX Burst and an action ability (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:75`). Lightning has EX Burst plus the zone-change trigger that the spec assigns to C2 (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:272`, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.md:26`). Cloud has a second attack-phase trigger with two protection effects (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:227`). Yet C1-A2 says no `unimplementedAbility` for any of the five (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.md:48`), and C1-9 excludes actions, EX Burst, and zone-change triggers (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.md:42`).
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.codex-review.md:31:None of the five effects needs a stack merely to calculate its result, so immediate resolution is a coherent MVP simplification. Cloud’s attack-phase trigger still needs an internal pause before attack declaration (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:227`; `packages/engine/src/phases.ts:50`). In real interaction, targeted ETBs also need a response window: for example, Lightning can target Undead Princess, but Undead Princess could put itself into the Break Zone as an action cost before Lightning resolves (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:136`, `packages/cards/data/cards.json:272`). Immediate resolution denies that response. Likewise, Ramuh could respond before Cloud’s pump or Shantotto’s protection resolves (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:45`, `packages/cards/data/cards.json:166`).
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.codex-review.md:99:**The 18-card census omits static/cost-modifying machinery from the C roadmap.**
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-c1-abilities.codex-review.md:101:Class Tenth Moogle changes produced CP (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:29`), Odin has conditional cost reduction (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:60`), and Sphene has static Break Zone protection (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:257`). None fits the listed C1/C2/C3 groups cleanly.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-25-mvp0-bones.codex-review.md:21:- **Tasks 5, 8, 9 — Concern:** `priority` is being used as “player who must make the next decision.” The defending player does not gain priority merely to declare a blocker; CR §10.1.2.6 and §10.1.3.6 instead give the turn player priority around those steps. This state shape will obstruct the planned stack/ability work. **Change:** Separate CR priority from pending decision ownership, e.g. `priority` plus `pending: { kind: 'declareBlock', player }`.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-25-mvp0-bones.codex-review.md:37:- **Task 8, `runRuleProcesses` — Concern:** CR §12.4.4 and §12.4.5 are conflated. A zero-power Character is put into the Break Zone, not broken; §12.4.5 applies the damage break process only at power 1000 or greater. The emitted `broken` event will later trigger the wrong abilities. **Change:** Model distinct zone-move reasons/events and implement the two thresholds separately.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-rung-a-heuristic-ai.codex-code-review.md:7:- **Affordable multi-element casts can be omitted.** Scarcity-first greedy assignment is not complete. For a three-element target and sources `{Earth}`, `{Earth, Lightning}`, `{Lightning, Fire}`, it can spend the second source on Earth after reserving the third for Fire, then fail Lightning although a legal matching exists. `preferredPayment` returns `null`, and `candidateCommands` silently drops the cast. `packages/ai/src/payment.ts:29-39`, `packages/ai/src/candidates.ts:44-48`. **Fix:** use bounded backtracking or minimum-cost bipartite matching for required elements, then greedily fill generic CP.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-26-rung-a-heuristic-ai.codex-code-review.md:9:- **Light/Dark casting violates CR §11.2.** `preferredPayment` requires a matching Light/Dark source, while CR §11.2.1.1/§11.2.2 exempts Light/Dark cards from the same-element requirement. Engine `canPay` also explicitly leaves the exemption unimplemented, so two off-element Backups cannot cast a cost-2 Light card. `packages/ai/src/payment.ts:29-36`, `packages/engine/src/cp.ts:37-42`. **Fix:** centralize required-element calculation in the engine, exempt single-element Light/Dark costs, and have both `canPay` and `preferredPayment` use it.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-25-mvp0-bones.md:19:- HIGH ×9: census corrected (see disagreement below); ESLint flat config added and `lint` in every verification; `apply` no longer requires `legalCommands` membership — every `applyX` self-validates, so legal non-minimal payments (§11.2.2.3) are accepted; Summon timing restriction declared as an MVP0 simplification; block/party-damage decisions modelled as `pending` decisions, `priority` stays the CR priority holder; `GameSession` adds command log + replay + undo with tests; `viewFor` returns a deep clone with an isolation test; self-play runs `checkInvariants` after every command; hotseat clears the screen and waits at each player change.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-25-mvp0-bones.md:41:- **Priority vs decisions:** `state.priority` is the CR §11.1 priority holder (in MVP0 always the turn player, since there is no stack). Step actions that the *other* player performs — declaring a blocker (§10.1.3.1), splitting party damage (§10.1.4.2.1) — and setup decisions are modelled as `state.pending = { kind, player }`, never by handing over priority. `actingPlayer(state) = pending?.player ?? priority`.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-25-mvp0-bones.md:43:- Deliberate MVP0 simplifications (each must be marked with a `// MVP0-SIMPLIFICATION:` comment where it lives, so later rungs can grep them): no stack, no priority passing (the non-turn player never holds priority), Summons may only be cast in Main Phases (§9.3.1.6 also allows the Attack Phase; those windows arrive with the stack), mulligan puts the hand back in hand order rather than a chosen order (§8.2.1.4), Attack Preparation and Damage Resolution steps auto-advance, Summons resolve to no effect, EX Burst on a damage-zone card is logged not resolved, a 6th Backup is simply illegal to cast (§7.7.4 first sentence) rather than handled by rule process §12.4.8, Light/Dark rules unimplemented (pool has none). Multi-Element cards (Shantotto 12-120C, Billy Bob 18-124C are Earth/Lightning) ARE in scope: casting them requires ≥1 CP of each element (§11.2.2.1).

Summons: pay, then straight to the owner's Break Zone with `summonResolvedNoEffect` (MVP0-SIMPLIFICATION — no stack). docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-code-review.md:185:    43	Running reduced ISMCTS on the main thread still invokes a pure synchronous search (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:467`) whose rollout cost is variable and only work-capped (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:53`). That would weaken the central non-blocking guarantee. Greedy is already the browser-safe, sub-millisecond path (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:11`, `apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:235`).
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-code-review.md:227:    85	`PlayerView` intentionally carries definitions (`packages/engine/src/view.ts:6`), the UI needs them for names and ability prompts (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:19`, `apps/web/src/game/commands.ts:73`), and all ability data is explicitly structured-cloneable (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:5`). The search already clones a state containing the same definitions once per determinisation (`packages/engine/src/determinise.ts:49`), so one extra request transfer of an 18-card catalogue is not the dominant cost.
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-code-review.md:284:    37	| D2-2 | **Decks and config at init; the view per request** | `PlayerView` carries `defs` by design and the UI needs them; the search already clones a state containing the same definitions once per determinisation, so one 18-card catalogue per request is not the dominant cost. Revision 1 called this "measured as negligible" — **it was not measured**; D2-A2 now reports the actual serialized size and posting duration, and `Omit<PlayerView,'defs'>` is revisited only if the catalogue materially grows. |
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-27-rung-d2-search-worker.codex-code-review.md:288:    41	| D2-6 | **Fall back to `GreedyAgent`, detect every way it can fail, and say so** | Greedy, not reduced-iteration main-thread ISMCTS: the latter is still a synchronous search with variable rollout cost, which gives up the one guarantee this rung exists for. Detection must cover **missing `Worker`, constructor failure, synchronous `postMessage` clone failure, `error`, `messageerror`, a typed `WorkerError`, and a worker that is killed or hangs and simply never replies** — the last needs a startup and per-request **watchdog**, because nothing correlated ever arrives. On failure: invalidate the request, terminate the worker, switch to Greedy **permanently for that game**, append **one** visible log warning, and play Greedy against the current state under the same pacing deadline. |

codex
A concrete contradiction has emerged: C3-A4 says a watcher must not fire, but the implemented C2 watcher is not “when broken”; it is “when put from the field into the Break Zone,” and its dispatcher deliberately ignores the transition reason. A self-break cost should therefore trigger Lightning even though it must not emit a break event or respect `cannotBeBroken`. I’m verifying the CR timing/citation before assigning severity.

## BLOCKER

**`Payment` is reusable, but the existing cast payment validator is not.**

`Payment` is only a description of CP sources (`packages/engine/src/commands.ts:4`), so retaining it is sound. But casting derives the amount and required Elements from the card definition (`packages/engine/src/cast.ts:33-37`), while Red Mage needs `1 + Lightning` despite having printed cost 2 (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:3-14`), and Miner needs generic 2—not Earth—despite having printed cost 3 (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:140-151`). `generateCp` also excludes `casting` only from discards (`packages/engine/src/cp.ts:33-35`), not from dulled Backups (`packages/engine/src/cp.ts:24-32`). Both Red Mage and Miner can therefore generate CP with themselves while also paying their `[Dull]`/self-break costs.

**Fix:** Keep `Payment`, but generalize the machinery around it to accept `{ amount, requiredElements, excludedSources }`. Apply exclusions to both Backup and discard sources, and use the same API from casting, enumeration, `preferredPayment`, and activation. Encode requirements as an Element array, not singular `element?`, so repeated/multi-Element costs do not require another fork. Generic `[2]` is `{ amount: 2, requiredElements: [] }`; `[Lightning]` is `{ amount: 1, requiredElements: ['lightning'] }`; `[0]` produces only the empty payment.

---

**The proposed command omits activation-time target legality, allowing a player to pay a cost for an ability they cannot activate.**

`resolve.ts` currently discovers targets after a frame starts and treats an empty set as a successful no-op (`packages/engine/src/resolve.ts:235-240`). That is correct for triggered abilities, but CR §11.6.5 says a targeted action ability needs a legal target before activation and cannot choose itself. Without a preflight, Undead Princess can break herself when she is the only Forward and get nothing; if checked before payment without `excludeSource`, she can illegally count herself as the target. [CR 3.3 §11.6.5](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

**Fix:** Make activation choices part of the activation transaction. Prefer `activateAbility { player, source, abilityId, payment, targets }`, validate targets against the pre-cost state with the source excluded, and initialize `Frame.chosen` accordingly. At minimum, preflight and snapshot the eligible set before payment; do not reuse the triggered-ability “no legal target → no-op” path.

---

**C3-A3 wrongly applies `[Dull]` restrictions to Undead Princess.**

The acceptance criterion says any dulled or newly entered source is illegal (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:86-89`), but those restrictions apply only when the cost contains the dull icon. Undead Princess’s first clause has only a self-to-Break-Zone cost (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:125-136`), so she may use it while dull and on the turn she enters. CR §11.6.2.2 applies the control-since-start/Haste rule specifically to abilities with `[Dull]`. [CR 3.3 §11.6.2.2](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

**Fix:** Gate active status, `enteredTurn`, and the Haste exception on `cost.dull === true`. Add positive tests that a dull/fresh Undead Princess can activate and that a fresh Noel with Haste can activate.

---

**C3-A4 contradicts C3-4: a self-break cost must trigger Lightning’s zone-movement watcher.**

C3-4 says the cost produces a `ZoneTransition` visible to C2 observers (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:56`), while C3-A4 says the observer must not fire (`:90-92`). The implemented observer is not “when broken”; its exact text is “put from the field into the Break Zone” (`packages/cards/src/abilities.ts:218-226`), and `watches` intentionally ignores `ZoneTransition.reason` (`packages/engine/src/resolve.ts:519-528`). It therefore must see Noel or Undead Princess paying this cost. What must not happen is a `broken`, `brokenByAbility`, or `breakPrevented` event. CR §15.1.1.3.2 explicitly says putting a card into the Break Zone as a cost is not breaking. [CR 3.3 §15.1.1.3.2](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

There is also an ordering requirement. `drainResolution` consumes its queue FIFO (`packages/engine/src/resolve.ts:413-430`). Cost-triggered auto-abilities go above the already-declared action ability and resolve first. Merely “pay, then push the frame” works only if the cost watcher frames are enqueued before the action frame.

**Fix:** Add `ZoneTransition.reason: 'cost'`. Snapshot the action frame’s source, controller, ability, targets, and the transition’s pre-cost `FieldCard` before mutation; apply every cost simultaneously; call `enqueueZoneChangeTriggers(pre, post, transitions)`; then append the action frame. True zone-movement observers fire; future explicitly “broken” observers filter out `reason: 'cost'`. Change `describeTriggerCause`, which currently says every zone move “was broken” (`apps/web/src/game/commands.ts:60-63`), to the accurate “was put into the Break Zone.”

---

**Miner’s effect cannot be represented by the current AST.**

`Effect` has no draw operation (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:53-73`). The only draw primitive is in `phases.ts` (`packages/engine/src/phases.ts:10-18`), while `resolve.ts` deliberately cannot import `phases.ts` because `phases.ts` already imports it (`packages/engine/src/resolve.ts:16-19`, `packages/engine/src/phases.ts:8`). The claim that all four effect halves need no new machinery is therefore false.

**Fix:** Add `{ kind: 'draw'; count: number }`, extract `drawCards` into a neutral module imported by both phases and resolution, and preserve its empty-deck loss semantics.

## MAJOR

**Main-phase-only activation is a real gameplay deviation, not merely a restatement of the current priority model.**

The CR permits action abilities in both Main and Attack Phases (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:47`; [CR 3.3 §9.3.1.7](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)). The engine actually has an unblocked turn-player action point during attack declaration (`packages/engine/src/legal.ts:68-72`), although it immediately resolves damage after a block and exposes no combat response window (`packages/engine/src/attack.ts:87-95`).

Noel and Red Mage still work before the first attack from Main Phase 1. Undead Princess does not work as the printed combat trick: she cannot pump after blockers, nor attack and then sacrifice herself to help a later attacker.

**Fix:** Either allow activation during attack declaration now and explicitly defer post-attack/block response windows, or retain main-only activation but document it as “action abilities are sorcery-speed; Undead Princess cannot be used as a combat trick.” Do not claim there is no further loss of fidelity.

---

**The AI does not receive activations “for free.”**

`candidateCommands` manually emits casts and pass in Main Phases (`packages/ai/src/candidates.ts:295-302`); SO-ISMCTS searches that list (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/search.ts:369`). An activation added only to `legalCommands` will never be considered by either agent. Action keys, decoding, and synthetic-ID guards also need explicit variants (`packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:202-237`, `packages/ai/src/ismcts/keys.ts:267-334`, `packages/ai/src/greedy.ts:186-199`).

The evaluation has two predictable mistakes:

- Backup status contributes nothing to material (`packages/ai/src/evaluate.ts:95-96`), so dulling Red Mage and other CP Backups can look free.
- With the current weights, losing active 2000-power Undead Princess is worth exactly 8, and giving another active Forward +4000 is also worth exactly 8 (`packages/ai/src/evaluate.ts:21-34`, `packages/ai/src/evaluate.ts:87-93`). Greedy retains the earlier command on a tie (`packages/ai/src/greedy.ts:95-107`), so activation ordering can make it sacrifice a body for a transient pump with no demonstrated payoff.

**Fix:** Explicitly generate one preferred-payment activation per `(source, abilityId, target set)`, add the ISMCTS codec/ID plumbing, and test that both agents actually choose an activation. Add a small active-Backup/ready-CP term and discount positive `powerBonus` when it cannot affect combat before expiry—especially Main Phase 2. Add “pass over useless Red Mage” and “pass over unusable Undead Princess pump” tests.

---

**Use stable `abilityId`, not an index into the implemented ability array.**

`Ability.id` already exists specifically as a stable per-clause identity (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:121-131`). Miner’s action is its printed second clause, but its deferred ETB is currently absent (`packages/cards/src/abilities.ts:40`). If the action is installed alone it occupies array index 0; adding the deck-knowledge ETB later shifts it. That is precisely rework created by the rung reordering.

**Fix:** Use `abilityId` in commands, frames, action keys, logs, and tests. Printed order remains the order of `def.abilities`; command identity must not depend on that position.

---

**Source zone belongs in the action-ability definition now.**

`Ability` currently has only a mandatory trigger and effects (`packages/engine/src/abilities.ts:121-132`), while the spec leaves the source-zone question unresolved (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:100-105`). Hard-coding `legalCommands` to scan fields will require another availability model immediately for the two hand abilities and again for Break-Zone abilities.

**Fix:** Add an action discriminant containing at least `sourceZone: 'field' | 'hand' | 'breakZone'` and cost metadata. Zone is an activation precondition, not part of the cost. Leave timing and once-per-turn extensions additive, but do not infer the source zone from a particular cost.

---

**The browser receives legal activations, but its usable one-choice UI does not come for free.**

The board already renders any field card appearing in `choices.byCard` as clickable (`apps/web/src/ui/Board.tsx:17-43`), so `Board.tsx` needs no special-case UI. But `describeChoice`, `subjectsOf`, and `sameCommand` have exhaustive command handling with no activation (`apps/web/src/game/commands.ts:225-254`, `:295-310`, `:349-369`). More importantly, `preferredChoices` collapses payment variants only for casts (`:372-420`); Red Mage or Miner would expose every enumerated payment as separate buttons.

**Fix:** Treat casts and activations as “payable commands” for payment collapsing, attach an activation to its source card in `subjectsOf`, compare `source + abilityId + targets + payment`, and render the printed cost plus chosen CP sources. Emit/narrate `abilityActivated`, not `abilityTriggered`; the latter currently produces “ability triggers” (`apps/web/src/game/useGame.ts:77-80`).

---

**C3-A6 misunderstands `ABILITY_CLAUSES`.**

`ABILITY_CLAUSES` stores the total number of printed clauses, implemented or not (`packages/cards/src/abilities.ts:21-30`). It must not “drop by four” as required by the spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:95-96`). Reducing Miner or Undead Princess from two to one would falsely hide their remaining deferred clauses. Missing warnings are derived from total minus `def.abilities.length` (`packages/engine/src/cast.ts:45-51`).

**Fix:** Keep every `ABILITY_CLAUSES` value unchanged. Assert that implemented AST count rises by four and the derived missing count falls by four.

## MINOR

**The two principal CR citations are wrong.**

CR §1 contains only the game-scope rule; cost atomicity is §11.6.10, activation procedure is §§11.6.3–11.6.11, and source independence is §11.5.4. The `[Dull]` control/Haste rule is §11.6.2.2, not §9.3.2 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:54-55`). The cost-versus-break distinction is §15.1.1.3.2. [Official CR 3.3](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

**Fix:** Replace the citations before turning them into code comments or test names.

---

**CR 3.3 permits over-generation, not overpayment.**

`cp.ts` says `apply` accepts overpayment (`packages/engine/src/cp.ts:54`), but CR §11.2.2.3 permits generating arbitrary CP, selecting exactly the required CP, and losing the remainder. The current `cp.length >= cost` representation can model this implicitly, but its terminology is misleading. [CR 3.3 §11.2.2.3](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

**Fix:** Document `Payment` as generated sources and `canPay` as proving a usable subset exists; call extras “unused generated CP.”

---

**The seeded reachability sweep is not enough for the new legality boundary.**

C3-A1 emphasizes driven games (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:80-82`), but rare combinations—fresh Noel with Haste, dull Undead Princess, no legal non-source target, cost-triggered Lightning—are unlikely to occur reliably.

**Fix:** Keep the sweep, but add constructed unit tests for every legality predicate, payment exclusion, transition reason, watcher order, and target-before-cost rollback.

## WHAT I WOULD DO DIFFERENTLY

**Keep activated abilities ahead of deck knowledge; the reordering is right.**

Deck knowledge still requires durable knowledge ownership, pending reconstruction, two search identities, and observer-relative narration (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c6-deck-knowledge.md:9-31`). None of the activation fixes above entangles determinisation with private information.

**Fix:** Keep deck knowledge deferred, but soften “eight clauses behind one primitive”: activation also needs target declaration, generalized costs, a draw effect, command codecs, and timing policy.

---

**Build the activation substrate first, then land cards in two small stages.**

The dangerous seam is not any individual AST; it is the transaction from activation declaration through simultaneous costs, cost triggers, and queued resolution (`packages/engine/src/apply.ts:25-57`).

**Fix:** Stage 1: action metadata/source zone, stable command identity, target preflight, generalized CP, atomic cost transitions, draw, agenda ordering, AI/UI codecs. Stage 2: Red Mage, Noel, Miner, and Undead Princess plus the adversarial tests.

---

**I would pull the two hand-sourced draw abilities into a short follow-up—or into this rung if scope allows.**

Once Miner forces `draw` and generalized action CP, Geomancer and Red Mage need only `sourceZone: 'hand'` plus `selfDiscard` (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:79-105`). They reveal themselves by immediately moving to the public Break Zone, so they do not require C6’s durable knowledge model. By contrast, Undead Princess’s second clause requires a new removed-from-play zone (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:16-23`), and Sphene requires field-to-Break-Zone history and once-per-turn state (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:245-257`).

**Fix:** Make source zone first-class now; preferably use the two hand clauses to prove it. Leave Break-Zone Undead Princess and Sphene in C4.

It must not “drop by four” as required by the spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:95-96`). Reducing Miner or Undead Princess from two to one would falsely hide their remaining deferred clauses. Missing warnings are derived from total minus `def.abilities.length` (`packages/engine/src/cast.ts:45-51`).

**Fix:** Keep every `ABILITY_CLAUSES` value unchanged. Assert that implemented AST count rises by four and the derived missing count falls by four.

## MINOR

**The two principal CR citations are wrong.**

CR §1 contains only the game-scope rule; cost atomicity is §11.6.10, activation procedure is §§11.6.3–11.6.11, and source independence is §11.5.4. The `[Dull]` control/Haste rule is §11.6.2.2, not §9.3.2 (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:54-55`). The cost-versus-break distinction is §15.1.1.3.2. [Official CR 3.3](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

**Fix:** Replace the citations before turning them into code comments or test names.

---

**CR 3.3 permits over-generation, not overpayment.**

`cp.ts` says `apply` accepts overpayment (`packages/engine/src/cp.ts:54`), but CR §11.2.2.3 permits generating arbitrary CP, selecting exactly the required CP, and losing the remainder. The current `cp.length >= cost` representation can model this implicitly, but its terminology is misleading. [CR 3.3 §11.2.2.3](https://fftcg.cdn.sewest.net/2026-08/fftcg-comprules-v3.3.pdf)

**Fix:** Document `Payment` as generated sources and `canPay` as proving a usable subset exists; call extras “unused generated CP.”

---

**The seeded reachability sweep is not enough for the new legality boundary.**

C3-A1 emphasizes driven games (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c3-activated-abilities.md:80-82`), but rare combinations—fresh Noel with Haste, dull Undead Princess, no legal non-source target, cost-triggered Lightning—are unlikely to occur reliably.

**Fix:** Keep the sweep, but add constructed unit tests for every legality predicate, payment exclusion, transition reason, watcher order, and target-before-cost rollback.

## WHAT I WOULD DO DIFFERENTLY

**Keep activated abilities ahead of deck knowledge; the reordering is right.**

Deck knowledge still requires durable knowledge ownership, pending reconstruction, two search identities, and observer-relative narration (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-rung-c6-deck-knowledge.md:9-31`). None of the activation fixes above entangles determinisation with private information.

**Fix:** Keep deck knowledge deferred, but soften “eight clauses behind one primitive”: activation also needs target declaration, generalized costs, a draw effect, command codecs, and timing policy.

---

**Build the activation substrate first, then land cards in two small stages.**

The dangerous seam is not any individual AST; it is the transaction from activation declaration through simultaneous costs, cost triggers, and queued resolution (`packages/engine/src/apply.ts:25-57`).

**Fix:** Stage 1: action metadata/source zone, stable command identity, target preflight, generalized CP, atomic cost transitions, draw, agenda ordering, AI/UI codecs. Stage 2: Red Mage, Noel, Miner, and Undead Princess plus the adversarial tests.

---

**I would pull the two hand-sourced draw abilities into a short follow-up—or into this rung if scope allows.**

Once Miner forces `draw` and generalized action CP, Geomancer and Red Mage need only `sourceZone: 'hand'` plus `selfDiscard` (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:79-105`). They reveal themselves by immediately moving to the public Break Zone, so they do not require C6’s durable knowledge model. By contrast, Undead Princess’s second clause requires a new removed-from-play zone (`packages/engine/src/state.ts:16-23`), and Sphene requires field-to-Break-Zone history and once-per-turn state (`packages/cards/data/cards.json:245-257`).

**Fix:** Make source zone first-class now; preferably use the two hand clauses to prove it. Leave Break-Zone Undead Princess and Sphene in C4.
